label: lem:linear-velocity
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Uniqueness follows from the $L^2$ energy estimate for the difference
of two solutions. To prove existence, let $\{V_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset D(A)$
be hydrostatic Stokes eigenfunctions satisfying $AV_k=\lambda_kV_k$.
They form an orthonormal basis of $H$ with respect to the
$L^2(\Omega)^2$ inner product and are orthogonal in $V$.
Let $P_m:H\to\operatorname{span}\{V_1,\ldots,V_m\}$ be the
$L^2$-orthogonal projection. For a fixed $m\in\mathbb N$, consider the Galerkin system,
\begin{align*}
\partial_t v^m
&+ P_m\mathbb{P}\Bigl(
    (v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_H)v^m
    + w^{n-1}\partial_z v^m
  \Bigr)
  - \mathbb{P}\Delta v^m
  \notag\\
&= -P_m\mathbb{P}(f_0 k\times v^m)
   +P_m\mathbb{P}\left(
      \nabla_H\int_{-h}^{z}T^*\,d\xi
    \right),\\
v^m(0)&=P_m v_0.
\end{align*}

Take the inner product of the first equation above with $V_k$. Denote $(v^m, V_k) = g_k(t)$, $\beta_{kj} = \left( \mathbb{P} \left[ (v^{n-1} \cdot \nabla_H) V_j + (w^{n-1} \partial_z) V_j \right], V_k \right)$,$\quad \alpha_{j,k} = (f_0 k \times V_j, V_k), \eta_k=(\nabla_H\int_{-h}^zT^*,V_k)$, therefore, we have
\begin{align*}
g_k'(t) + \lambda_k g_k(t) + \sum g_j (\beta_{kj}+\alpha_{jk}) &= \eta_k
\end{align*}
Let $g^m=(g_1,\dots,g_m)^{T}$,$\alpha^m=(\alpha_{ij})_{1\leq i,j \leq m}$, $\beta^m=(\beta_{ij})_{1\leq i,j \leq m}$, $\eta^m=(\eta_1,\dots,\eta_m)^T$ and $\Lambda^m$ is the diagonal matrix with $j$-th diagonal element $\lambda_j$
\begin{align*}
\partial_t g^m(t) + [\Lambda^m+\beta^m(t)+(\alpha^m)^T] g^m(t)  &= \eta^m\\
g^m(0)&={g^m_0}
\end{align*}

\noindent where $g_0^m=
\bigl((v_0,V_1)_{L^2},\ldots,(v_0,V_m)_{L^2}
\bigr)^{\mathsf T}$,$\int_0^{t_0}|\Lambda^m+\beta^m(s)+(\alpha^m(s))^T|ds<\infty$. Therefore, because of the ODE theory, it has the unique solution $v^m$ on $[0,t_0]$.
Under classic consideration, we may show $v^m$ is uniformly bounded in $X_{t_0}$ with respect to m. Therefore, by passing to a subsequence, there exists a $v$ such that $v^m \rightarrow v$, which is the solution of,
\begin{align*}
\partial_t v + \mathbb{P} \left( (v^{n-1} \cdot \nabla_H) v + (w^{n-1} \partial_z) v \right) + Av &= - \mathbb{P} (f_0 k \times v)+\mathbb{P}(\nabla_H \int_{-h}^zT^* d\xi) \\
v(0) &= v_0
\end{align*}
which implies that $v$ is the solution of the original equation.
head: environment

label: lem:linear-temperature
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:linear-temperature}
Let $t_0>0$ and suppose that
\[
v^{n-1}\in X_{t_0}
:=
L^\infty(0,t_0;V)
\cap
L^2(0,t_0;D(A)).
\]
\[
w^{n-1}(x,y,z,t)
:=
-\int_{-h}^{z}
\nabla_H\cdot v^{n-1}(x,y,\xi,t)\,d\xi .
\]
Then, for every $T_0\in V_T$, the problem
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:linear-temperature-original}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
\partial_tT^n
&+
(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_H)T^n
+
w^{n-1}\partial_zT^n
-
\Delta_HT^n
=0
&&\text{in }\Omega\times(0,t_0),\\
T^n&=0
&&\text{on }\Gamma_s\times(0,t_0),\\
T^n(\cdot,0)&=T_0
&&\text{in }\Omega
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
admits a unique solution satisfying
\[
T^n\in L^\infty(0,t_0;V_T),
\qquad
\nabla_HT^n\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega)),
\qquad
\partial_tT^n\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)).
\]
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:linear-temperature-L2}
\|T^n(t)\|_{L^2}^2
+2\int_0^t\|\nabla_HT^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
=\|T_0\|_{L^2}^2,
\qquad 0\leq t\leq t_0,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
&\sup_{0\leq t\leq t_0}
\|\nabla T^n(t)\|_{L^2}^2
\nonumber\\
&\quad+
\int_0^{t_0}
\left(
\|\Delta_HT^n(t)\|_{L^2}^2
+
\|\nabla_H\partial_zT^n(t)\|_{L^2}^2
\right)\,dt
\leq C_{n-1}(t_0)\|T_0\|_{H^1}^2,
\label{eq:linear-temperature-H1}
\end{align}
where $C_{n-1}(t_0)$ depends only on $\Omega$, $t_0$, and
\[
\|v^{n-1}\|_{L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1)}
+
\|v^{n-1}\|_{L^2(0,t_0;H^2)}.
\]
head: environment
name: The linear temperature equation

title: Proof:
body_md:
To define the
temperature projection $P_N^T$, let $\{\phi_j\}_{j\geq1}$ be the
$L^2(M)$-orthonormal basis of horizontal Dirichlet problem, ordered by nondecreasing eigenvalues, i.e.
\[
 -\Delta_H\phi_j=\lambda_j\phi_j\quad\hbox{in }M,
 \qquad \phi_j=0\quad\hbox{on }\partial M.
\]
In the vertical variable, use the $L^2(-h,0)$-orthonormal cosine basis
\[
 \chi_0(z)=h^{-1/2},\qquad
 \chi_k(z)=\sqrt{\frac2h}
       \cos\!\left(\frac{k\pi(z+h)}h\right),\quad k\geq1.
\]

Set $\mu_k=(k\pi/h)^2$ for $k\geq0$, so that
$-\chi_k''=\mu_k\chi_k$ and $\chi_k'(-h)=\chi_k'(0)=0$.
The products $\phi_j(x,y)\chi_k(z)$ form an orthonormal
basis of $L^2(\Omega)$. This basis is the analog of the  basis used by Saal and Slav\'ik
\cite[Eq.~(2.17)]{SaalSlavik2023}. For $N\geq1$, define
\[
 \mathcal E_N:=\operatorname{span}
 \{\phi_j\chi_k:1\leq j\leq N,\ 0\leq k\leq N\}.
\]
Let $P_N^T:L^2(\Omega)\to\mathcal E_N$ be the $L^2$-orthogonal
projection; explicitly,
\[
 P_N^Tf
 =\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{k=0}^N
    \left(\int_\Omega f(x,y,z)\phi_j(x,y)\chi_k(z)\,dx\,dy\,dz\right)
          \phi_j\chi_k.
\]

\[
 \|f\|_{H^1}^2
 =\sum_{j\geq1}\sum_{k\geq0}
 (1+\lambda_j+\mu_k)|(f,\phi_j\chi_k)|^2,
 \qquad f\in V_T,
\]
implies
\[
 \|P_N^Tf\|_{H^1}\leq\|f\|_{H^1},\qquad
 P_N^Tf\longrightarrow f\quad\text{in }H^1(\Omega).
\]
The Neumann condition satisfied by the basis is auxiliary:
this $H^1$ convergence imposes no vertical endpoint condition
on the limit.

We seek $T_N^n$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 (\partial_tT_N^n,\psi)
 +(\nabla_HT_N^n,\nabla_H\psi)
 &+(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n
       +w^{n-1}\partial_zT_N^n,\psi)=0,
 \qquad \psi\in\mathcal E_N,\\
 &T_N^n(0)=P_N^TT_0.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:linear-temperature-galerkin}
\end{equation}

This is a finite-dimensional linear system with integrable
time-dependent coefficients, and hence has a unique absolutely
continuous solution on $[0,t_0]$.
The divergence-free condition with boundary conditions gives,
\begin{equation}
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|T_N^n\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_HT_N^n\|_2^2=0.
 \label{eq:linear-temperature-approximate-L2}
\end{equation}
Testing \eqref{eq:linear-temperature-galerkin} by
$-\Delta_HT_N^n$ and $-\partial_{zz}T_N^n$, respectively, gives
\begin{align*}
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|\nabla_HT_N^n\|_2^2
       +\|\Delta_HT_N^n\|_2^2
 &=\bigl(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n
          +w^{n-1}\partial_zT_N^n,\Delta_HT_N^n\bigr),\\
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2
 &=-\bigl(\partial_zv^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n,
                                      \partial_zT_N^n\bigr)\\
 &\quad+\int_\Omega(\nabla_H\cdot v^{n-1})
                                  |\partial_zT_N^n|^2.
\end{align*}
By Lemma~\ref{anisotropic inequality}, for every $\delta>0$,
\begin{align*}
 \left|\bigl(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n
          +w^{n-1}\partial_zT_N^n,\Delta_HT_N^n\bigr)\right|
 &\leq\delta\bigl(\|\Delta_HT_N^n\|_2^2
                   +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2\bigr)\\
 &+C_\delta\|v^{n-1}\|_{H^2}^2
                                  \|\nabla_HT_N^n\|_2^2\\
 &+C_\delta\bigl(1+\|v^{n-1}\|_{H^1}^4
             +\|v^{n-1}\|_{H^1}^2\|v^{n-1}\|_{H^2}^2\bigr)
                                  \|\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
And,
\begin{align*}
 &\left|\bigl(\partial_zv^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n,
                                  \partial_zT_N^n\bigr)\right|
 +\left|\int_\Omega(\nabla_H\cdot v^{n-1})
                                  |\partial_zT_N^n|^2\right|\\
 &\quad\leq\delta\bigl(\|\Delta_HT_N^n\|_2^2
                   +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2\bigr)
 +C_\delta(1+\|v^{n-1}\|_{H^2}^2)\|\nabla T_N^n\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
Choosing $\delta$ sufficiently small therefore yields
\begin{equation}
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|\nabla T_N^n\|_2^2
 +\frac12\bigl(\|\Delta_HT_N^n\|_2^2
              +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2\bigr)
 \leq\Phi_{n-1}(t)\|\nabla T_N^n\|_2^2,
 \label{eq:linear-temperature-approximate-H1}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{n-1}(t)
 :=C\left[1+\|v^{n-1}(t)\|_{H^1}^4
 +(1+\|v^{n-1}(t)\|_{H^1}^2)
                          \|v^{n-1}(t)\|_{H^2}^2\right]
 \in L^1(0,t_0).
 \label{eq:Phi-n}
\end{equation}
Gronwall's inequality gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{0\leq t\leq t_0}\|T_N^n(t)\|_{H^1}^2
 +\int_0^{t_0}\bigl(\|\Delta_HT_N^n\|_2^2
                  +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT_N^n\|_2^2\bigr)\,dt\\
 &\hspace{30mm}\leq C_{n-1}(t_0)\|T_0\|_{H^1}^2.
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:linear-temperature-uniform}
\end{equation}
Here and below the constants are independent of $N$ and have
the dependence asserted in the lemma. Horizontal elliptic
regularity also bounds $\nabla_HT_N^n$ in $L^2(0,t_0;H^1)$.
Also,
\[
 \|\partial_tT_N^n\|_2
 \leq\|\Delta_HT_N^n\|_2
      +\|v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n\|_2
      +\|w^{n-1}\partial_zT_N^n\|_2.
\]
Using the anisotropic inequality in Lemma~\ref{anisotropic inequality},
\begin{equation}
 \|\partial_tT_N^n\|_{L^2(0,t_0;L^2)}
 \leq C_{n-1}(t_0)\|T_0\|_{H^1}.
 \label{eq:temperature-time-uniform}
\end{equation}

By Lemma~\ref{lem:aubin-lions} in Appendix \ref{app:analytic-tools}, the preceding estimates yield a subsequence such that
\begin{align*}
 T_N^n&\longrightarrow T^n
       &&\text{in }C([0,t_0];L^2),\\
 T_N^n&\rightharpoonup^*T^n
       &&\text{in }L^\infty(0,t_0;V_T),\\
 \nabla_HT_N^n&\rightharpoonup\nabla_HT^n
       &&\text{in }L^2(0,t_0;H^1),\\
 \partial_tT_N^n&\rightharpoonup\partial_tT^n
       &&\text{in }L^2(0,t_0;L^2).
\end{align*}
In particular, $T^n(0)=T_0$, and $T^n$ has zero lateral trace.

To pass to the limit in the equation, write
\[
 G_N=v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_HT_N^n
                  +w^{n-1}\partial_zT_N^n.
\]
The preceding estimates bound $G_N$ in $L^2(0,t_0;L^2)$.
For every smooth test function $\varphi$, integration by parts gives
\[
 \int_0^{t_0}(G_N,\varphi)\,dt
 =-\int_0^{t_0}
   (T_N^n,v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_H\varphi
                  +w^{n-1}\partial_z\varphi)\,dt.
\]
Strong $L^2$ convergence of $T_N^n$ and
$v^{n-1},w^{n-1}\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2)$ identify the limit of this expression. Testing the Galerkin equation by $P_N^T\varphi$
and using $P_N^T\varphi\to\varphi$ in $L^2(0,t_0;H^1)$
therefore yields
\begin{align*}
 &\int_0^{t_0}\!\int_\Omega
 \bigl[-T^n\partial_t\varphi
       +\nabla_HT^n\cdot\nabla_H\varphi\\
 &\hspace{28mm}-T^n(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_H\varphi
                    +w^{n-1}\partial_z\varphi)\bigr]
 =\int_\Omega T_0\varphi(\cdot,0)
\end{align*}
whenever $\varphi|_{\Gamma_s}=0$ and
$\varphi(\cdot,t_0)=0$.
The values of $\varphi$ at $z=-h,0$ are unrestricted.
Thus $T^n$ solves \eqref{eq:linear-temperature-original}.

Weak lower semicontinuity yields
\eqref{eq:linear-temperature-H1}. The uniform $H^1$ bound and
$T^n\in C([0,t_0];L^2)$ give a weakly $H^1$-continuous
representative, so that the supremum can be taken over all
$t\in[0,t_0]$.
The transport bounds also hold for $T^n$, and hence every term
of its equation belongs to $L^2(0,t_0;L^2)$.
Therefore, we could multiply the equation by $T^n$, and derive the uniqueness and \eqref{eq:linear-temperature-L2}.
head: environment

label: prop:vn-L2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:vn-L2}
Assume that $(v_0,T_0)\in V\times V_T$. Then, for every $n\geq1$ and $t>0$,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+\int_0^t\|\nabla v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
\leq 2K_1(t),
\label{eq:v-energy}
\end{equation}
where
\[
K_1(t):=
\|v_0\|_{L^2}^2+C_h t\|T_0\|_{L^2}^2,
\]
and $C_h>0$ depends only on $h$. In particular, the bound is
independent of $n$.
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Multiply the velocity equation by $v^n$, the transport and surface pressure terms vanish by incompressibility, the hydrostatic divergence constraint, and the boundary conditions. The Coriolis term also vanishes since $(k\times v^n)\cdot v^n=0$. It follows by the Cauchy Schwarz inequality, and Young's inequality,
\begin{align*}
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|v^n\|_{L^2}^2
+\|\nabla v^n\|_{L^2}^2
&=-\int_\Omega
\left(\int_{-h}^zT^n(\xi)\,d\xi\right)
\nabla_H\cdot v^n\,dx\\
&\leq\frac12\|\nabla v^n\|_{L^2}^2
+C\|T^n\|_{L^2}^2,
\end{align*}
Using \eqref{eq:linear-temperature-L2} and integrating in time, we obtain, for every $s\in[0,t]$,
\[
\|v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+\int_0^s\|\nabla v^n(\tau)\|_{L^2}^2\,d\tau
\leq
\|v_0\|_{L^2}^2+C_hs\|T_0\|_{L^2}^2
=K_1(s).
\]
Since $K_1$ is nondecreasing and both terms on the left are nonnegative, it follows that
\[
\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\leq K_1(t),
\qquad
\int_0^t\|\nabla v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds\leq K_1(t).
\]
Adding these inequalities yields \eqref{eq:v-energy}.
head: environment

label: eq:T-Lq
title: Remark
body_md:
If, in addition, $T_0\in L^p(\Omega)$ for some $2\leq p\leq\infty$,
then
\begin{equation}
\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|T^n(s)\|_{L^p}
\leq\|T_0\|_{L^p},
\qquad n\geq1,\quad t>0.
\label{eq:T-Lq}
\end{equation}
Indeed, for $2\leq p<\infty$, multiply temperature equation with $|T^n|^{p-2}T^n$ and integrate to give
\[
\frac1p\frac{d}{dt}\|T^n\|_{L^p}^p
+(p-1)\int_\Omega|T^n|^{p-2}|\nabla_HT^n|^2\,dx
=0.
\]
Thus $H^1$ initial data ensures $T_0 \in L^6$, while additional $L^p$ integrability of the initial temperature gives the corresponding $L^p$ estimate for any larger exponent, the case $p=\infty$ follows by letting $p\to\infty$ when $T_0\in L^\infty(\Omega)$.
head: manual
name: $L^p$ estimates for the temperature

label: thm:A^1/2 v
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: thm:H1 T
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
The estimates for $v^n$ and $T^n$ are coupled. More precisely, the
higher-order estimate for $v^n$ involves the $H^1$-estimate of $T^n$,
whereas the latter depends only on the estimates of $v^{n-1}$.
Therefore, we prove the two propositions simultaneously by induction
on $n$.

For convenience, define
\begin{equation}
E_v^n(t)
:=
\sup_{0\le s\le t}
\|A^{1/2}v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+
\int_0^t
\|Av^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds,
\label{eq:Ev-definition}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
E_T^n(t)
:=
\sup_{0\le s\le t}
\|\nabla T^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+
\int_0^t
\left(
\|\Delta_H T^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+
\|\nabla_H\partial_zT^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
\right)\,ds.
\label{eq:ET-definition}
\end{equation}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Step 1. A conditional estimate for $T^n$.}
Let $K_2>0$ be a constant to be fixed in Step~2, and suppose that
\begin{equation}
E_v^{n-1}(t)\leq K_2,
\qquad 0\leq t\leq t^*\leq1.
\label{eq:conditional-velocity-bound}
\end{equation}
The temperature estimate follows directly from the calculation in
Lemma~\ref{lem:linear-temperature}. Indeed, by the norm equivalences
for $A$ and \eqref{eq:Phi-n},
\[
\int_0^t\Phi_{n-1}(s)\,ds
\leq C\bigl[(1+K_2^2)t+(1+K_2)K_2\bigr].
\]
Applying Gronwall's inequality to
\eqref{eq:linear-temperature-approximate-H1} and passing to the limit
as in that lemma therefore gives
\begin{equation}
E_T^n(t)\leq K_3(t)
:=2\|\nabla T_0\|_{L^2}^2
\exp\!\left\{C\bigl[(1+K_2^2)t+(1+K_2)K_2\bigr]\right\},
\label{eq:conditional-temperature-bound}
\end{equation}
where $C$ depends only on $\Omega$. Here the factor $2$ accounts for
the time supremum and the integrated dissipation. In particular,
for fixed $K_2$, this bound is independent of $n$ and
$tK_3(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$.
We fix $K_2$ and close the joint induction in Step~2.

\medskip
\noindent
\textbf{Step 2. The higher-order estimate for $v^n$.}
We now derive the higher-order estimate for $v^n$. A direct
higher-order energy estimate is not sufficient because of the mismatch
of indices in the approximation scheme. We therefore introduce the
decomposition
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:velocity-decomposition}
v^n=\widetilde V+\widetilde v^n,
\qquad
w^n=\widetilde W+\widetilde w^n,
\end{equation}
where $\widetilde V$ is independent of $n$ and solves
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:linear-V}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\widetilde V
-\Delta\widetilde V
+\nabla_H\widetilde P_s
+f_0k\times\widetilde V
&=0
&&\text{in }\Omega\times(0,t^*),\\
\nabla_H\cdot\int_{-h}^{0}\widetilde V\,dz
&=0
&&\text{in }M,\\
\partial_z\widetilde V&=0
&&\text{on }\Gamma_t,\\
\widetilde V&=0
&&\text{on }\Gamma_b\cup\Gamma_s,\\
\widetilde V(\cdot,0)&=v_0
&&\text{in }\Omega.
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
The corresponding vertical velocity is defined by
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:linear-W}
\widetilde W(x,y,z,t)
:=
-\int_{-h}^{z}
\nabla_H\cdot\widetilde V(x,y,\xi,t)\,d\xi .
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
\widetilde W=0
\qquad\text{on }\Gamma_t\cup\Gamma_b.
\]

For each $n\geq0$, we also set
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:remainder-w}
\widetilde w^n(x,y,z,t)
:=
-\int_{-h}^{z}
\nabla_H\cdot\widetilde v^n(x,y,\xi,t)\,d\xi .
\end{equation}
Then
\[
w^n=\widetilde W+\widetilde w^n.
\]

We choose the initial iterate to be the linear solution:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:initial-iterate}
v^0:=\widetilde V,
\qquad
w^0:=\widetilde W.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:initial-remainder}
\widetilde v^0=0,
\qquad
\widetilde w^0=0.
\end{equation}
Notice that every iterate has the same initial value:
\[
v^n(\cdot,0)=v_0,
\qquad n\geq0,
\]
and hence
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:remainder-zero-initial}
\widetilde v^n(\cdot,0)=0,
\qquad n\geq0.
\end{equation}

Testing the projected form of \eqref{eq:linear-V} with
$\widetilde V$ and $A\widetilde V$, respectively, gives
\begin{align*}
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
+\|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
&=0,\\
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
+\|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
&=-f_0(k\times\widetilde V,A\widetilde V)_{L^2}\\
&\leq\frac12\|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
+\frac{f_0^2}{2}\|\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2.
\end{align*}
The first identity implies
$\|\widetilde V(t)\|_{L^2}\leq\|v_0\|_{L^2}$.
Integrating the second inequality therefore yields, for
$0\leq t\leq t^*\leq1$,
\begin{align}
E_{\widetilde V}(t)
&:=\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|A^{1/2}\widetilde V(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+\int_0^t\|A\widetilde V(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
\nonumber\\
&\leq2\|A^{1/2}v_0\|_{L^2}^2
+2f_0^2\|v_0\|_{L^2}^2=:C_V.
\label{eq:CV-definition}
\end{align}
Moreover, since
$\partial_t\widetilde V=-A\widetilde V
-\mathbb{P}(f_0k\times\widetilde V)$, we have
\begin{equation}
\int_0^t\|\partial_t\widetilde V(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
\leq2\int_0^t\|A\widetilde V(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
+2f_0^2t\|v_0\|_{L^2}^2.
\label{eq:linear-V-time}
\end{equation}

We now derive the equation satisfied by the remainder.
Using
\[
v^{n-1}
=
\widetilde V+\widetilde v^{n-1},
\qquad
w^{n-1}
=
\widetilde W+\widetilde w^{n-1},
\]
and subtracting \eqref{eq:linear-V} from the $n$-th velocity
equation, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:remainder-equation}
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\widetilde v^n
-\Delta\widetilde v^n
+\nabla_H\widetilde p_s^n
+f_0k\times\widetilde v^n
={}&
-\bigl(
  (\widetilde V+\widetilde v^{n-1})\cdot\nabla_H
 \bigr)
 (\widetilde V+\widetilde v^n)
\\
&-
(\widetilde W+\widetilde w^{n-1})
\partial_z(\widetilde V+\widetilde v^n)
+\nabla_H Q_T^n
&&\text{in }\Omega\times(0,t^*),\\
\nabla_H\cdot\int_{-h}^{0}\widetilde v^n\,dz
={}&0
&&\text{in }M,\\
\partial_z\widetilde v^n={}&0
&&\text{on }\Gamma_t,\\
\widetilde v^n={}&0
&&\text{on }\Gamma_b\cup\Gamma_s,\\
\widetilde v^n(\cdot,0)={}&0
&&\text{in }\Omega,
\end{aligned}
\right.
\end{equation}
where
\[
\widetilde p_s^n:=p_s^n-\widetilde P_s.
\]

The essential point is that the higher-order energy of
$\widetilde v^n$ vanishes initially. We therefore define
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:remainder-energy}
E_{\widetilde v}^n(t)
:=
\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+
\int_0^t
\|A\widetilde v^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds.
\end{equation}

Fix
\[
K_2:=2(C_V+1).
\]
We prove by induction that, for a sufficiently small $t^*>0$
independent of $n$,
\begin{equation}
E_{\widetilde v}^n(t^*)\leq1,
\qquad n\geq0.
\label{eq:remainder-induction-goal}
\end{equation}
The case $n=0$ follows from \eqref{eq:initial-remainder}.
Assume the bound holds for $n-1$. Then, for $0\leq t\leq t^*$,
\[
E_v^{n-1}(t)
\leq2E_{\widetilde V}(t)+2E_{\widetilde v}^{n-1}(t)
\leq K_2,
\]
so Step~1 gives $E_T^n(t)\leq K_3(t)$.

For $a,b\in D(A)$, let
$w(a):=-\int_{-h}^z\nabla_H\cdot a(\xi)\,d\xi$.
The Sobolev embeddings and the anisotropic product estimate,
together with the norm equivalences for $A$, give
\[
\|(a\cdot\nabla_H)b+w(a)\partial_zb\|_{L^2}^2
\leq C\|A^{1/2}a\|_{L^2}\|Aa\|_{L^2}
       \|A^{1/2}b\|_{L^2}\|Ab\|_{L^2}.
\]
Testing \eqref{eq:remainder-equation} by $A\widetilde v^n$,
expanding the transport terms, and applying this estimate and
Young's inequality, we obtain
\begin{align*}
&\frac{d}{dt}\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^n\|_{L^2}^2
+\|A\widetilde v^n\|_{L^2}^2\\
&\quad\leq C\Bigl(
1+\|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2\|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
+\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}^2
 \|A\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}^2\Bigr)
\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^n\|_{L^2}^2\\
&\qquad+C\Bigl[
\|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2\|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
+\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}
 \|A\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}
 \|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}\|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}
+\|\nabla_HT^n\|_{L^2}^2\Bigr].
\end{align*}
Here and below $C$ depends only on $\Omega$ and $f_0$.
Set
\[
\rho(t):=\int_0^t\|A\widetilde V(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds.
\]
Since $\widetilde V$ is fixed, $\rho(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$.
The induction hypothesis and the bound for $\widetilde V$ imply
\begin{align*}
\int_0^t\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}^2
             \|A\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
&\leq1,\\
\int_0^t\|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2
             \|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
&\leq C_V\rho(t),\\
\int_0^t\|A^{1/2}\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}
             \|A\widetilde v^{n-1}\|_{L^2}
             \|A^{1/2}\widetilde V\|_{L^2}
             \|A\widetilde V\|_{L^2}\,ds
&\leq\sqrt{C_V\rho(t)}.
\end{align*}
Consequently, Gronwall's inequality and the zero initial value of
$\widetilde v^n$ yield
\[
E_{\widetilde v}^n(t)
\leq C\exp\!\bigl\{C[t+C_V\rho(t)+1]\bigr\}
\Bigl[C_V\rho(t)+\sqrt{C_V\rho(t)}+tK_3(t)\Bigr].
\]
The right-hand side is independent of $n$ and tends to zero as
$t\downarrow0$. We may therefore choose $t^*\in(0,1]$ so that it
is at most $1$ at $t=t^*$. This closes the induction. Finally,
\[
E_v^n(t^*)\leq2(C_V+1)=K_2,
\qquad
E_T^n(t^*)\leq K_3(t^*),
\]
which proves both propositions.

label: prop:iteration-time-regularity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:iteration-time-regularity}
Let $(v^n,T^n)$ be the iterates constructed above, and let
$0<t^*\leq1$ be such that \eqref{eq:uniform-vn-H1} and
\eqref{eq:uniform-Tn-H1} hold. Then there exists a constant $K_4$,
independent of $n$, such that
\[
 \int_0^{t^*}\left(
       \|\partial_tv^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2
       +\|\partial_tT^n(s)\|_{L^2}^2\right)\,ds
 \leq K_4.
\]
head: environment
name: Time regularity

title: Proof:
body_md:
The temperature estimate follows from the time-derivative argument
in Lemma~\ref{lem:linear-temperature}, leading to
\eqref{eq:temperature-time-uniform}. Indeed, inserting
\eqref{eq:uniform-vn-H1} and \eqref{eq:uniform-Tn-H1} into that
argument gives, for the limiting iterate,
\[
 \int_0^{t^*}\|\partial_tT^n\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
 \leq C(1+K_2)K_3(t^*).
\]
Here the velocity bound also holds for the initial iterate $v^0$
by its construction, so the constant is uniform for all $n\geq1$.

Applying the hydrostatic Helmholtz projection to the velocity
equation gives
\begin{align*}
 \partial_tv^n+Av^n
 ={}&-\mathbb P\bigl[(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_H)v^n
              +w^{n-1}\partial_zv^n+f_0k\times v^n\bigr]\\
 &+\mathbb P\left(\int_{-h}^z\nabla_HT^n\,d\xi\right).
\end{align*}
The transport estimate used in the joint proof of
Propositions~\ref{thm:A^1/2 v} and~\ref{thm:H1 T}, together with
Cauchy--Schwarz in time and \eqref{eq:uniform-vn-H1}, yields
\[
 \int_0^{t^*}
 \|(v^{n-1}\cdot\nabla_H)v^n
                +w^{n-1}\partial_zv^n\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
 \leq CK_2^2.
\]
Since $\mathbb P$ is an $L^2$ contraction, the projected equation
and the uniform spatial estimates imply
\[
 \int_0^{t^*}\|\partial_tv^n\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
 \leq C\bigl[(1+t^*)K_2+K_2^2+t^*K_3(t^*)\bigr].
\]
Combining the two estimates proves the assertion with
\[
 K_4=C(1+K_2)\bigl[K_2+K_3(t^*)\bigr],
\]
where $C$ depends only on the fixed parameters.

label: prop:iteration-convergence
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:iteration-convergence}
After decreasing the common existence time $t^*>0$ if necessary,
the entire sequence $(v^n,T^n)$ converges strongly in
\[
 \bigl(C([0,t^*];V)\cap L^2(0,t^*;D(A))\bigr)
 \times
 \bigl(C([0,t^*];L^2(\Omega))
       \cap L^2(0,t^*;L^2((-h,0);H_0^1(M)))\bigr).
\]
In particular, $v^{n-1}$ and $v^n$ converge to the same velocity.
head: environment
name: Strong convergence of the iteration

label: eq:joint-iteration-difference-system
title: Proof:
body_md:
For $n\geq2$, denote $U^n:=v^n-v^{n-1},\Theta^n:=T^n-T^{n-1}, w(U^n):=-\int_{-h}^z\nabla_H\cdot U^n(\xi)\,d\xi.$
Starting at $n=2$ avoids introducing a temperature iterate $T^0$.
Write $B(a,f):=a\cdot\nabla_Hf+w(a)\partial_zf$. Subtracting consecutive projected velocity equations and temperature equations gives
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:joint-iteration-difference-system}
 \begin{aligned}
 \partial_tU^{n+1}+AU^{n+1}
       +\mathbb P B(v^n,U^{n+1})
       +\mathbb P(f_0k\times U^{n+1})
 &=-\mathbb P B(U^n,v^n)
       +\mathbb P\left(\nabla_H\int_{-h}^z\Theta^{n+1}(\xi)\,d\xi\right),\\
 \partial_t\Theta^{n+1}-\Delta_H\Theta^{n+1}
       +B(v^n,\Theta^{n+1})
 &=-B(U^n,T^n),
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
with $(U^{n+1},\Theta^{n+1})(0)=0$ and the inherited homogeneous boundary conditions. We multiply the velocity equation and temperature equation by $AU^{n+1}$ and $\Theta^{n+1}$ respectively, and let 
\[
 M_T:=\sup_{n\geq1}\|T^n\|_{L^\infty(0,t^*;H^1)}<\infty,
\]
In the temperature equation, For every $\eta>0$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |(U^n\cdot\nabla_HT^n,\Theta^{n+1})|
 &\leq CM_T\|AU^n\|_2\|\Theta^{n+1}\|_2\\
 &\leq\eta\|AU^n\|_2^2+C_\eta M_T^2\|\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2,
 \end{aligned}
\]
using anisotropic estimates, we obtain,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |(w(U^n)\partial_zT^n,\Theta^{n+1})|
 &\leq CM_T\|A^{1/2}U^n\|_2^{1/2}\|AU^n\|_2^{1/2}
           \|\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^{1/2}
           \|\nabla_H\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^{1/2}\\
 &\leq\tfrac14\|\nabla_H\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2
       +\eta\|AU^n\|_2^2
       +C_\eta M_T^2\bigl(\|A^{1/2}U^n\|_2^2
                              +\|\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
$\eta>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:joint-iteration-temperature-energy}
 \frac{d}{dt}\|\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_H\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2
 \leq\eta\|AU^n\|_2^2
       +C_\eta M_T^2\bigl(\|A^{1/2}U^n\|_2^2
                              +\|\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2\bigr).
\end{equation}

For the velocity equation, use the estimate from the joint proof of Propositions~\ref{thm:A^1/2 v} and~\ref{thm:H1 T},
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:joint-iteration-velocity-energy}
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{d}{dt}\|A^{1/2}U^{n+1}\|_2^2+\|AU^{n+1}\|_2^2
 &\leq
 C\bigl(1+\|A^{1/2}v^n\|_2^2\|Av^n\|_2^2\bigr)
                         \|A^{1/2}U^{n+1}\|_2^2\\
 &+C_\eta\|A^{1/2}v^n\|_2^2\|Av^n\|_2^2
                         \|A^{1/2}U^n\|_2^2
       +\eta\|AU^n\|_2^2
       +C_0\|\nabla_H\Theta^{n+1}\|_2^2.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $C_0$ is fixed independently of $\eta$ and $n$.
Choose a fixed $\kappa\geq\max\{1,2C_0\}$ and define
\[
 Y_n:=\|A^{1/2}U^n\|_2^2+\kappa\|\Theta^n\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 D_n:=\|AU^n\|_2^2+\frac\kappa2\|\nabla_H\Theta^n\|_2^2.
\]
Multiplying \eqref{eq:joint-iteration-temperature-energy} by
$\kappa$, adding \eqref{eq:joint-iteration-velocity-energy}, and
choosing $\eta$ in terms of $\varepsilon>0$, we obtain
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:joint-iteration-combined-energy}
 Y_{n+1}'+D_{n+1}
 \leq G_{n,\varepsilon}(t)(Y_{n+1}+Y_n)+\varepsilon D_n,
 \qquad
 G_{n,\varepsilon}
 :=C_\varepsilon\bigl(1+M_T^2+
             \|A^{1/2}v^n\|_2^2\|Av^n\|_2^2\bigr).
\end{equation}
The decomposition $v^n=\widetilde V+\widetilde v^n$ implies
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:joint-iteration-small-dissipation}
 r(t):=\sup_{n\geq0}\int_0^t\|Av^n(s)\|_2^2\,ds
 \leq2\int_0^t\|A\widetilde V(s)\|_2^2\,ds+2\sup_{n\geq0}E_{\widetilde v}^n(t)
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
For $0<\tau\leq t^*$, set
\[
 E_{\mathrm{diff}}^n(\tau)
 :=\sup_{0\leq s\leq\tau}Y_n(s)+\int_0^\tau D_n(s)\,ds,
 \qquad
 \mu_\varepsilon(\tau)
 :=C_\varepsilon\bigl[(1+M_T^2)\tau+K_2r(\tau)\bigr].
\]
By \eqref{eq:uniform-vn-H1},
$\int_0^\tau G_{n,\varepsilon}(s)\,ds
\leq\mu_\varepsilon(\tau)$ uniformly in $n$. Apply Gronwall's inequality to Equation~\eqref{eq:joint-iteration-combined-energy},
\[
 E_{\mathrm{diff}}^{n+1}(\tau)
 \leq2e^{\mu_\varepsilon(\tau)}
       \bigl[\varepsilon+\mu_\varepsilon(\tau)\bigr]
       E_{\mathrm{diff}}^n(\tau).
\]
Choosing \(\varepsilon>0\) sufficiently small and then \(\tau\in(0,t^*]\) sufficiently small, independently of \(n\), we obtain
\[
E_{\mathrm{diff}}^{n+1}(\tau)\le \frac{1}{4}\,E_{\mathrm{diff}}^n(\tau),
\qquad n\ge2,
\]
Thus the entire sequences are Cauchy in the stated spaces, with time continuity following from the time-derivative bounds. Replacing \(t^*\) by \(\tau\) proves the assertion. In particular, \(v^n\) and \(v^{n-1}\) converge strongly to the same limit.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $v_0\in V$ and $T_0\in V_T(\Omega)$, then system~\eqref{eq:primitive-momentum}--\eqref{eq:primitive-initial-data} has a strong solution $(v,T)$
in $\Omega\times(0,t^*)$, where $t^*$ is the same positive time stated in the previous propositions.
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
We use the common time $t^*$ after the possible reduction in
Proposition~\ref{prop:iteration-convergence}. All preceding
uniform estimates remain valid on this interval.
By Propositions~\ref{thm:A^1/2 v}, \ref{thm:H1 T},
and~\ref{prop:iteration-time-regularity}, for all $n$, 
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{0\leq t\leq t^*}
\left(
\|v^n\|_{H^1}^2
+\|T^n\|_{H^1}^2
\right)
+\int_0^{t^*}
\left(
\| v^n\|_{H^2}^2
+\|\nabla_H T^n\|_{H^1}^2
\right)\,dt
\leq C ,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\int_0^{t^*}
\left(
\|\partial_t v^n\|_{L^2}^2
+
\|\partial_t T^n\|_{L^2}^2
\right)\,dt
\leq C ,
\end{equation}
where $C$ is a constant independent of $n$.

In view of the above uniform estimates, Lemma~\ref{lem:aubin-lions} yields a subsequence,
still denoted by $\{(v^n,T^n)\}$, and a pair $(v,T)$ such that
\begin{align}
(v^n,T^n) &\to (v,T)
&& \text{in } C([0,t^*];L^2(\Omega)), \label{eq:iteration-strong-C-L2}\\
(\nabla v^n,\nabla_H T^n) &\to (\nabla v,\nabla_H T)
&& \text{in } L^2(0,t^*;L^2(\Omega)), \label{eq:iteration-strong-gradient-L2}\\
(v^n,T^n) &\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup} (v,T)
&& \text{in } L^\infty(0,t^*;H^1(\Omega)), \label{eq:iteration-weak-star-H1}\\
(\nabla v^n,\nabla_H T^n) &\rightharpoonup
(\nabla v,\nabla_H T)
&& \text{in } L^2(0,t^*;H^1(\Omega)), \label{eq:iteration-weak-gradient-H1}\\
(\partial_t v^n,\partial_t T^n) &\rightharpoonup
(\partial_t v,\partial_t T)
&& \text{in } L^2(\Omega\times(0,t^*)). \label{eq:iteration-weak-time-derivatives}
\end{align}
Here, $\rightharpoonup$ and $\overset{*}{\rightharpoonup}$ denote the weak
and weak-* convergences, respectively.
Moreover, Proposition~\ref{prop:iteration-convergence} shows that
the entire velocity sequence converges in $X_{t^*}$. Hence the
preceding iterates also satisfy
\[
 v^{n-1}\longrightarrow v\qquad\text{strongly in }X_{t^*}.
\]
Thus the transporting velocities and the velocity iterates
have the same limit. By virtue of
\eqref{eq:iteration-strong-C-L2}--\eqref{eq:iteration-weak-time-derivatives}, we may pass to the limit in the approximate system and
conclude that $(v,T)$ is a strong solution to the original system on
$(0,t^*)$.

By the local construction and the uniqueness estimate in
Proposition~\ref{prop:strong-solution-stability}, the solution extends
to a unique maximal strong solution on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$.
Suppose that $\mathcal T^*<\infty$.
Propositions~\ref{prop:appendix-basic-energy},
\ref{prop:appendix-velocity-L6-vertical},
\ref{prop:appendix-velocity-H1}, and
\ref{prop:appendix-temperature-H1} give bounds that remain finite
as $t\uparrow\mathcal T^*$. Consequently,
\[
\begin{gathered}
v\in L^\infty(0,\mathcal T^*;V)
       \cap L^2(0,\mathcal T^*;D(A)),\\
T\in L^\infty(0,\mathcal T^*;V_T),\qquad
\nabla_HT\in L^2(0,\mathcal T^*;H^1(\Omega)).
\end{gathered}
\]
Applying to the original equations the same product estimates used in Proposition~\ref{prop:iteration-time-regularity}, we obtain
\[
v_t\in L^2(0,\mathcal T^*;H),\qquad
T_t\in L^2(0,\mathcal T^*;L^2(\Omega)).
\]
The Hilbert-space trace theorem
\cite{LionsMagenes1972}, together with
$D(A^{1/2})=V$, gives
\[
 L^2(0,\mathcal T^*;D(A))
 \cap H^1(0,\mathcal T^*;H)
 \hookrightarrow
 C([0,\mathcal T^*];D(A^{1/2}))
 =C([0,\mathcal T^*];V).
\]
Together with
\[
 T\in H^1(0,\mathcal T^*;L^2(\Omega))
 \hookrightarrow C([0,\mathcal T^*];L^2(\Omega)),
\]
this yields the limits
\[
v(t)\longrightarrow v_*\quad\text{in }V,\qquad
T(t)\longrightarrow T_*\quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega)
\quad\text{as }t\uparrow\mathcal T^*.
\]
The uniform $H^1$ bound for $T$ and the weak closedness of $V_T$
imply $T_*\in V_T$.

Applying the local construction at time $\mathcal T^*$ with initial
data $(v_*,T_*)\in V\times V_T$ gives a strong solution on
$[\mathcal T^*,\mathcal T^*+\delta]$ for some $\delta>0$.
The matching $L^2$ time traces allow this solution to be joined to
the preceding one; the joined solution satisfies the equations
distributionally and retains all the regularity required in
Definition~\ref{def:strong-solution}. It is therefore a strong solution
beyond $\mathcal T^*$, contradicting maximality.
Thus $\mathcal T^*=\infty$, which, together with uniqueness, proves
Theorem~\ref{thm:global-well-posedness}.

label: prop:strong-solution-stability

name: Uniqueness and continuous dependence

title: Proof:
body_md:
For $i=1,2$, recall the vertical velocity is given by
\[
 w^{(i)}(z)=-\int_{-h}^z\nabla_H\cdot v^{(i)}(\xi)\,d\xi.
\]
The differences inherit all the boundary conditions. The estimates below are rigorously justified at level of theorem \ref{thm:global-well-posedness} with the regularity in Definition~\ref{def:strong-solution}. Indeed, both differences
belong to $H^1(0,t_0;L^2)$, so their squared $L^2$ norms are absolutely continuous and satisfy the Hilbert-space chain rule.
Subtract the two equations, retain $(v^{(1)},w^{(1)})$ as the
transporting velocity, and multiply by $v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}$ and $T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}$, respectively. Similarly as the $L^2$ energy estimates, it follows that
\begin{align*}
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(
       \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_2^2
       +\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^2\Bigr)
 &+\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_H(T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\|_2^2\\
 &=-\int_\Omega
       \bigl((v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\cdot\nabla_H\bigr)v^{(2)}
                           \cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\\
 &\quad-\int_\Omega(w^{(1)}-w^{(2)})\partial_zv^{(2)}
                           \cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\\
 &\quad+\int_\Omega\left(
       \int_{-h}^z\nabla_H(T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})(\xi)\,d\xi\right)
                           \cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\\
 &\quad-\int_\Omega
       \bigl((v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\cdot\nabla_HT^{(2)}\bigr)
                           (T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\\
 &\quad-\int_\Omega(w^{(1)}-w^{(2)})\partial_zT^{(2)}
                           (T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}).
\end{align*}
For any $\eta>0$, H\"older's inequality, Sobolev embedding, and Poincar\'e's
inequality give
\begin{align*}
 &\left|\int_\Omega
       \bigl((v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\cdot\nabla_H\bigr)v^{(2)}
                           \cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\right|\\
 &\quad\leq\|\nabla_Hv^{(2)}\|_3
                           \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_3^2\\
 &\quad\leq\eta\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
       +C_\eta\|v^{(2)}\|_{H^2}^2
                           \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_2^2,
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
 &\left|\int_\Omega
       \bigl((v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\cdot\nabla_HT^{(2)}\bigr)
                           (T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\right|\\
 &\quad\leq\|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_6
       \|\nabla_HT^{(2)}\|_3\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2\\
 &\quad\leq\eta\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
       +C_\eta\|\nabla_HT^{(2)}\|_{H^1}^2
                           \|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
 &\left|\int_\Omega\left(
       \int_{-h}^z\nabla_H(T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})(\xi)\,d\xi\right)
                           \cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\right|\\
 &\quad\leq C_h\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2
                           \|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2\\
 &\quad\leq\eta\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
       +C_\eta\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^2.
\end{align*}

To estimate the two vertical transport terms, use anisotropic inequality Lemma~\ref{anisotropic inequality},
\begin{align*}
 &\left|\int_\Omega(w^{(1)}-w^{(2)})\partial_zv^{(2)}
                           \cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\right|\\
 &\quad\leq C\|v^{(2)}\|_{H^1}^{1/2}
              \|v^{(2)}\|_{H^2}^{1/2}
              \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_2^{1/2}
              \|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^{3/2}\\
 &\quad\leq\eta\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
       +C_\eta\|v^{(2)}\|_{H^1}^2\|v^{(2)}\|_{H^2}^2
                           \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
For the temperature term, the anisotropic inequality yields,
\begin{align*}
 &\left|\int_\Omega(w^{(1)}-w^{(2)})\partial_zT^{(2)}
                           (T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\right|\\
 &\quad\leq C\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2
          \|\partial_zT^{(2)}\|_2^{1/2}
          \Bigl(\|\partial_zT^{(2)}\|_2^{1/2}
                +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT^{(2)}\|_2^{1/2}\Bigr)\\
 &\hspace{30mm}\cdot\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^{1/2}
          \|\nabla_H(T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\|_2^{1/2}\\
 &\quad\leq\eta\Bigl(
          \|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
          +\|\nabla_H(T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\|_2^2\Bigr)\\
 &\qquad+C_\eta\|\partial_zT^{(2)}\|_2^2
          \Bigl(\|\partial_zT^{(2)}\|_2^2
                +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT^{(2)}\|_2^2\Bigr)
                           \|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
Choose $\eta$ sufficiently small so that all the gradient terms could be absorbed, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:coupled-stability-differential}
\begin{split}
 \frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(
       \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_2^2
       +\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^2\Bigr)
 &+\|\nabla(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_H(T^{(1)}-T^{(2)})\|_2^2\\
 &\leq G(t)\Bigl(
       \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_2^2
       +\|T^{(1)}-T^{(2)}\|_2^2\Bigr).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
The coefficient is integrable using only
\[
 v^{(2)}\in L^\infty_tH^1\cap L^2_tH^2,\qquad
 \partial_zT^{(2)}\in L^\infty_tL^2,\qquad
 \nabla_HT^{(2)}\in L^2_tH^1.
\]
Gronwall's inequality followed by integration of
\eqref{eq:coupled-stability-differential} proves
\eqref{eq:coupled-strong-stability}. The $L^2$ time continuity of both solutions guarantees the initial and terminal values in the estimate.

label: thm:higher-regularity
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:higher-regularity}
Given a positive number $t_0$. Let $v_0 \in D(A) $ and $T_0 \in H^2(\Omega)\cap V_T$ be two functions, then there exists a unique strong solution to system~\eqref{eq:primitive-momentum}--\eqref{eq:primitive-initial-data} on $\Omega \times (0,t_0)$ with the following regularity,  for every $\epsilon\in(0,1)$,
\[
v \in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^2(\Omega))
\cap C([0,t_0];H^1(\Omega)),
\quad  v \in L^2(0,t_0;H^{3-\epsilon}(\Omega)),
\]
\[
T \in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^2(\Omega))
\cap C([0,t_0];H^1(\Omega)),
\quad
\nabla_H T \in L^2(0,t_0;H^{2}(\Omega)),
\]
\[
\partial_t v \in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega)),
\qquad
\partial_t T \in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega));
\]
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: On nonsmooth domains, solutions of the Stokes system generally do not enjoy the same regularity as on smooth domains because of corner singularities, which prevent us from obtaining higher-order regularity such as $v\in H^3(\Omega)$ and $p\in H^2(\Omega)$, even when the forcing term is sufficiently smooth. Higher-order regularity depends on the corner and edge geometry and on the boundary conditions, and may require additional compatibility conditions on the data; see \cite{MazyaRossmann2007}. Since no compatibility assumptions of this type are imposed in the present work, we do not discuss $H^3$-regularity of the solution.

label: prop:time-derivative-L2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:time-derivative-L2}
Under the initial-data assumptions of this section, there exists a continuous nondecreasing function $M_4$, finite on compact subintervals
of $[0,\mathcal T^*)$, such that
\[
 \mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}_{0<s<t}
 \left(\|v_t(s)\|_{L^2}^2+\|T_t(s)\|_{L^2}^2\right)
 +\int_0^t\left(\|\nabla v_t(s)\|_{L^2}^2
                    +\|\nabla_HT_t(s)\|_{L^2}^2\right)\,ds
 \leq M_4(t).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Fix $0<t_0<\mathcal T^*$ and choose $\eta_0>0$ such that
$t_0+\eta_0<\mathcal T^*$. We use the existing strong solution
from Section~\ref{sec:construction-global}. For $0<\eta<\eta_0$, set
\[
 \delta_\eta v(t):=\frac{v(t+\eta)-v(t)}{\eta},
 \qquad
 \delta_\eta T(t):=\frac{T(t+\eta)-T(t)}{\eta}.
\]
We first bound the initial difference quotients.

Let $w_0=-\int_{-h}^z\nabla_H\cdot v_0(\xi)\,d\xi$.
The anisotropic estimates give,
\[
 \|w_0\partial_zv_0\|_2+\|w_0\partial_zT_0\|_2
 \leq C\|v_0\|_{H^2}
             \bigl(\|v_0\|_{H^2}+\|T_0\|_{H^2}\bigr).
\]
Hence $(F_0^v,F_0^T)$ defined following belong to $L^2(\Omega)$:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &F_0^v:=Av_0+\mathbb P\left[
       (v_0\cdot\nabla_H)v_0+w_0\partial_zv_0+f_0k\times v_0
       -\int_{-h}^z\nabla_HT_0(\xi)\,d\xi\right],\\
 &F_0^T=-\Delta_HT_0+v_0\cdot\nabla_HT_0+w_0\partial_zT_0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Choose sufficiently large $C_0 \geq \max \{1,\| F_0^v \|_{L^2},\| F_0^T \|_{L^2},e^{G(0)|_{(v_0,T_0)}}\}$, which only depends on $\| v_0 \|_{H^2}$ and $\| T_0 \|_{H^2}$. $G(0)|_{(v_0,T_0)}$ is the value in \eqref{eq:coupled-stability-coefficient} evaluated at $(v_0,T_0)$.

Subtract the $F_0^v$ and $F_0^T$ from the velocity and temperature equation,
\begin{align*}
\partial_t(v-v_0)+A(v-v_0)
+\mathbb P\Bigg[
  &v\cdot\nabla_H(v-v_0)+w\partial_z(v-v_0)\\
  &+(v-v_0)\cdot\nabla_Hv_0
    +(w-w_0)\partial_zv_0\\
  &+f_0k\times(v-v_0)
    -\int_{-h}^{z}\nabla_H(T-T_0)(\xi)\,d\xi
\Bigg]
&=-F_0^v,\\[1mm]
\partial_t(T-T_0)-\Delta_H(T-T_0)
  &+v\cdot\nabla_H(T-T_0)+w\partial_z(T-T_0)\\
  &+(v-v_0)\cdot\nabla_HT_0
    +(w-w_0)\partial_zT_0
=- F_0^T.
\end{align*}
And repeat the energy calculation in the Uniqueness proof in Proposition~\ref{prop:strong-solution-stability}, we obtain,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac{d}{dt}\bigl(\|v(t)-v_0\|_2^2+\|T(t)-T_0\|_2^2\bigr)
 &\leq
 C_0\bigl(\|v(t)-v_0\|_2^2+\|T(t)-T_0\|_2^2\bigr)\\
 &+2C_0
       \bigl(\|v(t)-v_0\|_2^2+\|T(t)-T_0\|_2^2\bigr)^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Set
\[
Y(t):=\|v(t)-v_0\|_2^2+\|T(t)-T_0\|_2^2.
\]
Then we have the differential form $Y'(t)\leq C_0 Y+2 C_0 Y^{\frac{1}{2}}$.

Since $v,T\in H^1(0,t_0+\eta_0;L^2(\Omega))$,
\[
Y'(t)
=2\bigl(v(t)-v_0,v_t(t)\bigr)_{L^2}
 +2\bigl(T(t)-T_0,T_t(t)\bigr)_{L^2}
\quad\text{for a.e. }t.
\]
The right-hand side belongs to $L^1(0,t_0+\eta_0)$, so $Y$ is absolutely continuous. The initial traces give $Y(0)=0$.
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:sqrt-gronwall} to the differential inequality $Y'(t)\leq C_0 Y+2 C_0 Y^{\frac{1}{2}}$, we obtain
\[
\sqrt{Y(t)}\leq C_0t\,e^{C_0t/2}.
\]
Consequently, for $0<\eta<\eta_0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\delta_\eta v(0)\|_2^2+\|\delta_\eta T(0)\|_2^2
=\frac{Y(\eta)}{\eta^2}\leq C_0^2e^{C_0\eta}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Now apply Uniqueness Proposition~\ref{prop:strong-solution-stability} to
$(v(t+\eta),T(t+\eta))$ and $(v(t),T(t))$ on $[0,t_0]$.
Let $G(t)$ be the expression in
\eqref{eq:coupled-stability-coefficient} with
$(v^{(2)},T^{(2)})=(v(t),T(t))$, which is independent of $\eta$ and belongs to $L^1(0,t_0)$ by theorem~\ref{thm:global-well-posedness}.
Dividing \eqref{eq:coupled-strong-stability} by $\eta^2$ and
controlling the supremum and the dissipation integral separately,
we obtain, for $0\leq t\leq t_0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
       \bigl(\|\delta_\eta v(s)\|_2^2
                         +\|\delta_\eta T(s)\|_2^2\bigr)&+\int_0^t
       \bigl(\|\nabla\delta_\eta v\|_2^2
                         +\|\nabla_H\delta_\eta T\|_2^2\bigr)\,ds\\
 &\leq 2C_0^2\exp\!\left(C_0\eta+\int_0^tG(s)\,ds\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $v,T\in H^1(0,t_0+\eta_0;L^2)$, their time
difference quotients are the Steklov averages of $v_t,T_t$.
By the strong convergence of Steklov averages
(see \cite[Chapter~I, Lemma~3.2]{DiBenedetto1993}
and \cite[Lemma~2.5]{AmbrosioCiani2026}), we obtain
\[
(\delta_\eta v,\delta_\eta T)\longrightarrow(v_t,T_t)
\quad\text{strongly in }L^2(0,t_0;L^2)
\quad\text{as }\eta\downarrow0.
\]
The uniform bounds above identify the weak limits of the spatial
gradients with $\nabla v_t$ and $\nabla_HT_t$, and the weak-star
limits in $L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2)$ with $v_t,T_t$.
Lower semicontinuity therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}_{0<s<t}
       \bigl(\|v_t(s)\|_2^2+\|T_t(s)\|_2^2\bigr) +\int_0^t
       \bigl(\|\nabla v_t\|_2^2+\|\nabla_HT_t\|_2^2\bigr)\,ds
 \leq2C_0^2\exp\!\left(\int_0^tG(s)\,ds\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
The right-hand side defines a continuous nondecreasing $M_4$ on
$[0,\mathcal T^*)$.

label: prop:velocity-H2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:velocity-H2}
For every $0<t_0<\mathcal T^*$, there is a continuous nondecreasing
function $M_5$ on $[0,t_0]$ such that
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|v(s)\|_{H^2}^2\leq M_5(t),
 \qquad 0\leq t\leq t_0.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Recall $v\in L^2(0,t_0;D(A))$ and $v_t\in L^2(0,t_0;V)$, then
\[
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|A^{3/4}v\|_2^2
   =(A^{1/2}v_t,Av)_{L^2}.
\]
It gives,
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|A^{3/4}v(s)\|_2^2
 \leq\|A^{3/4}v_0\|_2^2
       +2\|A^{1/2}v_t\|_{L^2(0,t;L^2)}\|Av\|_{L^2(0,t;L^2)}.
\]
The initial term is finite because $v_0\in D(A)$. By interpolation, and
Lemma~\ref{lemma:Gagliardo}\textup{(ii)},
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D(A^{3/4})
   &=[D(A^{1/2}),D(A)]_{1/2}\\
   &\hookrightarrow[H^1(\Omega)^2,H^2(\Omega)^2]_{1/2}
     =H^{3/2}(\Omega)^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus $v\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^{3/2}(\Omega))$.
Also,
\[
 \|w\|_{L^\infty_zH^{1/2}(M)}
       +\|\partial_zv\|_{L^2_zH^{1/2}(M)}
 \leq C\|v\|_{H^{3/2}(\Omega)}.
\]
Using $H^{1/2}(M)\hookrightarrow L^4(M)$,
$H^1(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^6(\Omega)$,
$H^{1/2}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^3(\Omega)$, we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|(v\cdot\nabla_H)v+w\partial_zv\|_2
 &\leq \|v\|_6\|\nabla_Hv\|_3
       +\|w\|_{L^\infty_zL^4(M)}\|\partial_zv\|_{L^2_zL^4(M)}\\
 &\leq C\|v\|_{H^{3/2}}^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:top-stokes-H2} in the constant-depth case to
the momentum equation. Vertical integration of the thermal forcing
then yields, for almost every time,
\[
 \|v\|_{H^2}
 \leq C\bigl(\|v_t\|_2+\|v\|_{H^{3/2}}^2
                         +\|v\|_2+\|\nabla_HT\|_2\bigr).
\]
Every term on the right is uniformly bounded by the preceding
estimates. The known $H^1$ continuity of $v$ and weak lower
semicontinuity extend this bound to every time.

label: lem:flat-vertical-temperature
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{lem:flat-vertical-temperature}
\label{prop:Tzz-estimate}
Let $v_0\in D(A)$ and $T_0\in H^2(\Omega)\cap V_T$, and let $(v,T)$ be the unique global strong solution given by Theorem~\ref{thm:global-well-posedness}. Recall, for every $0<t_0<\mathcal T^*$, we have 
\[
\begin{aligned}
T
&\in L^\infty(0,t_0;V_T),
&
\nabla_HT
&\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega)),
\\
T_t
&\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)),
&
\nabla_HT_t
&\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then the same solution has the additional regularity
\[
\partial_z^2T\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)),
\qquad
\nabla_H\partial_z^2T
\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)).
\]
More precisely, there exists a continuous nondecreasing
function $M_7$ on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$, finite on subintervals, such that
\begin{equation}
\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
\|\partial_z^2T(s)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2
+
\int_0^t
\|\nabla_H\partial_z^2T(s)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\,ds
\leq M_7(t)
\label{eq:Tzz-bound}
\end{equation}
for every $0\leq t<\mathcal T^*$.

label: eq:flat-vertical-coefficients
title: Proof:
body_md:
Fix $0<t_0<\mathcal T^*$. We use the temperature Galerkin spaces and projection $P_N^T$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:linear-temperature},
and write $\mathcal E_N:=\operatorname{ran}P_N^T$. Recall,
\[
 \partial_z w=-\nabla_H\cdot v,\qquad
 \partial_{zz}w=-\nabla_H\cdot\partial_zv,\qquad
 w|_{z=-h,0}=0.
\]
By Sobolev embedding and trace theorems, we have $H^{3/4}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^\infty_zH^{1/4}(M)
\hookrightarrow L^\infty_zL^{8/3}(M)$, which implies,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\|v\|_\infty+\|w\|_\infty+\|\partial_zv\|_\infty
       +\|\partial_zw\|_\infty+\|\partial_{zz}v\|_3\\
 &\qquad+\|\partial_{zz}w\|_{L^\infty_zL^{8/3}_H}
       \leq C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}.
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:flat-vertical-coefficients}
\end{equation}
Differentiating the temperature equation \eqref{eq:T equation} in $z$ yields
\[
 (\partial_zT)_t-\Delta_H\partial_zT
 +v\cdot\nabla_H\partial_zT+\partial_z(w\partial_zT)
 =-\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT
\]
in the sense of distributions. The existing $\partial_zT$ belongs to
$L^\infty_tL^2\cap L^2_tL^2_zH_0^1(M)$; Its initial trace is $\partial_zT_0$ weakly in $L^2$, since $T\in C([0,t_0];L^2)$ and is uniformly bounded in $H^1$. Recall the temperature projection defined in lemma~\ref{lem:linear-temperature}, with the given $v,w,T$ fixed, solve the finite-dimensional linear system
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\bigl(\partial_t(\partial_zT)_N,\psi\bigr)
   +\bigl(\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N,\nabla_H\psi\bigr)\\
 &\quad+\bigl(v\cdot\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N
                  +\partial_z(w(\partial_zT)_N),\psi\bigr)
   =-\bigl(\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT,\psi\bigr),\\
 &(\partial_zT)_N(0)=P_N^T(\partial_zT_0),
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:flat-vertical-regularized}
\end{equation}
for every $\psi\in\mathcal E_N$. Parentheses denote the
$L^2(\Omega)$ inner product. For each $N$, the matrix coefficients
are integrable in time and the forcing belongs to $L^2$ in time;
the linear system therefore has a unique absolutely continuous
solution on $[0,t_0]$. $(\partial_zT)_N$ denotes the solution of this auxiliary system.
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 P_N^T(\partial_zT_0)\longrightarrow\partial_zT_0
                         \quad\hbox{in }H^1(\Omega),\\
 \|\partial_zP_N^T(\partial_zT_0)\|_2
                              \leq\|\partial_{zz}T_0\|_2,\qquad
 \partial_zP_N^T(\partial_zT_0)\longrightarrow\partial_{zz}T_0
                         \quad\hbox{in }L^2(\Omega).
 \end{gathered}
\]

Mutiply the Galerkin system with $(\partial_zT)_N$ and $-\partial_{zz}(\partial_zT)_N$. Moreover,
$\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N=0$ at $z=-h,0$. Integration by parts gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\\
 &\quad=-\bigl(\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT,(\partial_zT)_N\bigr)
       -\int_\Omega\partial_zw\,|(\partial_zT)_N|^2
 \end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2
       +\|\nabla_H\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\\
 &\quad=-\bigl(\partial_z(\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT),
                                      \partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\bigr)\\
 &\qquad-\bigl(\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N,
                                      \partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\bigr)\\
 &\qquad-2\int_\Omega\partial_zw\,
                                      |\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N|^2\\
 &\qquad-\bigl(\partial_{zz}w\,(\partial_zT)_N,
                                      \partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
By \eqref{eq:flat-vertical-coefficients}, $H^1(\Omega)\hookrightarrow
L^6(\Omega)$, and $H^1(M)\hookrightarrow L^8(M)$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\|\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT\|_2
       +\|\partial_z(\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT)\|_2
       \leq C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}\|\nabla_HT\|_{H^1},\\
 &\|\partial_{zz}w\,(\partial_zT)_N\|_2
       \leq C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}
          \bigl(\|(\partial_zT)_N\|_2
                    +\|\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N\|_2\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Adding the two energy estimates and absorbing the terms containing $\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}\|\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N\|_2 \|\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2$ yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(1+\|(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2
                          +\|\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\bigr)\\
 &\quad+\|\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2
             +\|\nabla_H\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\\
 &\leq C\bigl(1+\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}^2
                       +\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}\|\nabla_HT\|_{H^1}\bigr)\\
 &\qquad\cdot\bigl(1+\|(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2
                          +\|\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The coefficient is integrable by Section~\ref{sec:construction-global}
and Proposition~\ref{prop:velocity-higher-spatial} with
$\varepsilon=1/4$, and the initial energy is bounded by
$1+\|\partial_zT_0\|_2^2+\|\partial_{zz}T_0\|_2^2$.
Gronwall's inequality therefore gives uniform bounds for
$(\partial_zT)_N$ and $\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N$ in
$L^\infty_tL^2$, and for their horizontal gradients in $L^2_tL^2$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:flat-vertical-regularized}, written in divergence
form, also bounds $\partial_t(\partial_zT)_N$ in $L^2(0,t_0;V_T')$.
Here $V_T'$ is the dual of the scalar temperature space $V_T$,
with pivot $L^2(\Omega)$.
Indeed, the projection is bounded on that space,
$v,w,\partial_zw\in L^2_tL^\infty$, and
$\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT\in L^2_tL^2$ by
$T\in L^\infty_tH^1$ and \eqref{eq:flat-vertical-coefficients}.
Aubin--Lions and weak compactness give, along a subsequence,
\[
 (\partial_zT)_N\longrightarrow(\partial_zT)_*
       \quad\hbox{strongly in }L^2_tL^2
       \quad\hbox{and in }C([0,t_0];L^2\hbox{-weak}).
\]
The derivative bounds pass weakly to this limit. It remains to identify this limit with $\partial_zT$. Let
\[
d=(\partial_zT)_*-\partial_zT,
\qquad
P(x,y,z,t)=\int_{-h}^{z}d(x,y,\xi,t)\,d\xi.
\]
Subtracting the two equations gives,
\[
d_t-\Delta_Hd+v\cdot\nabla_Hd+\partial_z(wd)=0,
\]
with zero initial data in the weak $L^2$ sense. The preceding
bounds imply
\[
P\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega))
       \cap L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega)),
\qquad
\partial_zP=d\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)),
\]
and $P$ has zero lateral boundary condition. Let $\chi_a$ be a vertical cutoff of width
$a$, with $|\chi_a'|\leq C/a$. Since
\[
|w(z)|\leq
\operatorname{dist}(z,\{-h,0\})\|\partial_zw\|_\infty,
\]
for any smooth test function $\varphi$,
\[
\left|
\int_0^{t_0}\int_\Omega wd\,\chi_a'\varphi
\right|
\leq C_\varphi a^{1/2}
\|\partial_zw\|_{L^1_tL^\infty}
\|d\|_{L^\infty_tL^2}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
Testing with the backward vertical primitive of a smooth test
function and applying Fubini's theorem therefore yields
\[
P_t-\Delta_HP+v\cdot\nabla_HP+w\partial_zP=\mathcal K_v P,
\qquad
\mathcal K_v P(z)
:=\int_{-h}^{z}
\partial_zv(\xi)\cdot\nabla_HP(\xi)\,d\xi.
\]

Horizontal integration by parts, the embedding $H_0^1(M)\hookrightarrow L^8(M)$, and the identity $\nabla_H\cdot\partial_zv=-\partial_{zz}w$ give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\mathcal K_v P\|_{\mathcal V_H'}
&\leq C\left(
\|\partial_zv\|_\infty
+\|\partial_{zz}w\|_{L^\infty_zL^{8/3}(M)}
\right)\|P\|_2\\
&\leq C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}\|P\|_2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, $\mathcal K_v P\in L^2(0,t_0;\mathcal V_H')$. The equation and the preceding bounds then imply
\[
P_t\in L^2(0,t_0;\mathcal V_H').
\]
Since $P\in L^2(0,t_0;\mathcal V_H)$, it follows that $P\in C([0,t_0];L^2)$ and that its $L^2$ energy identity is valid. The weak initial condition gives $P(0)=0$.

Testing the equation with $P$, the transport terms cancel by $\nabla_H\cdot v+\partial_zw=0$ and the boundary conditions.
Moreover,
\[
\|\mathcal K_v P\|_2
\leq C_h\|\partial_zv\|_\infty\|\nabla_HP\|_2.
\]
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|P\|_2^2+\|\nabla_HP\|_2^2
&=(\mathcal K_v P,P)\\
&\leq
C_h\|\partial_zv\|_\infty\|\nabla_HP\|_2\|P\|_2\\
&\leq
\frac12\|\nabla_HP\|_2^2
+C\|\partial_zv\|_\infty^2\|P\|_2^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\partial_zv\in L^2(0,t_0;L^\infty)$ and $P(0)=0$, Gronwall's inequality gives $P=0$. Thus
\[
d=\partial_zP=0,
\qquad
(\partial_zT)_*=\partial_zT.
\]
The uniform derivative bounds therefore pass to the original solution, yielding
\[
\partial_{zz}T\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2),
\qquad
\nabla_H\partial_{zz}T\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2).
\]
The identified limit belongs to $L^2_tH^1$ and has time derivative
in $L^2$ in time with values in the dual of the lateral-zero $H^1$
space. Its $L^2$ energy identity is therefore valid. Compare it
with the first Galerkin energy identity. The forcing terms converge
by strong $L^2_tL^2$ convergence. The terms containing
$\partial_zw\,|(\partial_zT)_N|^2$ converge because
$\partial_zw\in L^2_tL^\infty$ and the approximations are uniformly
bounded in $L^\infty_tL^2$. Weak convergence at the terminal time
and lower semicontinuity then give
\[
 \nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N\longrightarrow\nabla_H\partial_zT
                    \quad\hbox{strongly in }L^2_tL^2.
\]
Returning to the second Galerkin energy identity, without absorbing the horizontal gradient of $(\partial_zT)_N$, gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(1+\|\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\bigr)
       +2\|\nabla_H\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\\
 &\quad\leq C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}
       \bigl(1+\|\nabla_HT\|_{H^1}+\|(\partial_zT)_N\|_2
                         +\|\nabla_H(\partial_zT)_N\|_2\bigr)\\
 &\hspace{24mm}\cdot
       \bigl(1+\|\partial_z(\partial_zT)_N\|_2^2\bigr).
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:flat-vertical-energy}
\end{equation}
By the two strong convergences above and Cauchy--Schwarz in time,
the coefficient on the right converges in $L^1(0,t_0)$ to
\[
 C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}
       \bigl(1+\|\nabla_HT\|_{H^1}+\|\partial_zT\|_2
                                 +\|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_2\bigr).
\]
This is bounded by
\[
 C\|v\|_{H^{11/4}}
       \bigl(1+\|T\|_{L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1)}
                                 +\|\nabla_HT\|_{H^1}\bigr).
\]
Also,
$\partial_zP_N^T(\partial_zT_0)\to\partial_{zz}T_0$ in $L^2$.
Applying Gronwall's inequality to \eqref{eq:flat-vertical-energy}, integrate, and passing to the limit proves \eqref{eq:flat-vertical-temperature-bound}. 
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
       \|\partial_{zz}T(s)\|_2^2
       +\int_0^t\|\nabla_H\partial_{zz}T\|_2^2\,ds\\
 &\qquad\leq C\bigl(1+\|\partial_{zz}T_0\|_2^2\bigr)
        \exp\!\Bigg(C\int_0^t\|v(s)\|_{H^{11/4}}\\
 &\hspace{16mm}\cdot\bigl(1+\|T\|_{L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1)}
             +\|\nabla_HT(s)\|_{H^1}\bigr)\,ds\Bigg),
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:flat-vertical-temperature-bound}
\end{equation}
where $C$ depends only on $M$ and $h$.

label: prop:horizontal-temperature-L2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:horizontal-temperature-L2}
There exists a continuous nondecreasing function $M_6$ on
$[0,\mathcal T^*)$ such that
\[
\|\Delta_HT\|_{L^\infty(0,t;L^2(\Omega))}\leq M_6(t)
\qquad\text{for every }0<t<\mathcal T^*.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Fix $0<t<\mathcal T^*$. Theorem \ref{thm:global-well-posedness}
and Propositions~\ref{prop:time-derivative-L2},
\ref{prop:velocity-H2}, and~\ref{prop:Tzz-estimate} give
\[
\begin{gathered}
T\in L^\infty(0,t;H^1),\qquad
T_t\in L^\infty(0,t;L^2),\\
v\in L^\infty(0,t;H^2),\qquad
\partial_z^2T\in L^\infty(0,t;L^2).
\end{gathered}
\]
Moreover, $\Delta_HT\in L^2(0,t;L^2)$ is already known. Hence horizontal Dirichlet elliptic regularity and Lemma~\ref{lem:anisotropic-isotropic} with $s=2$ imply, for almost every time,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_2
&\leq \|T\|_{H^2}\\
&\leq C\bigl(
\|\Delta_HT\|_2+\|T\|_{H^1}+\|\partial_z^2T\|_2
\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

The anisotropic Lemma~\ref{anisotropic inequality} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|w\partial_zT\|_2^2
&\leq C\|v\|_{H^1}\|v\|_{H^2}
\|\partial_zT\|_2
\bigl(\|\partial_zT\|_2+\|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_2\bigr)\\
&\leq C\bigl(1+\|\Delta_HT\|_2\bigr),
\end{aligned}
\]
where $C$ after the second inequality depends only on the preceding bounds and the domain, which is independent of the time. Therefore, the temperature equation, Sobolev embedding, and Young's inequality give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Delta_HT\|_2
&\leq \|T_t\|_2
+\|v\|_\infty\|\nabla_HT\|_2
+\|w\partial_zT\|_2\\
&\leq C\bigl(1+\|\Delta_HT\|_2^{1/2}\bigr)\\
&\leq \frac12\|\Delta_HT\|_2+C,
\end{aligned}
\]
for almost every time in $(0,t)$. Absorbing the first term on the right and taking the essential
supremum yields
\[
\|\Delta_HT\|_{L^\infty(0,t;L^2)}\leq 2C.
\]
The preceding estimates admit continuous nondecreasing majorants,
and the constants above depend only on these majorants and the
fixed domain. They therefore provide the required function
$M_6(t)$.

label: prop:vertical-temperature-time
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:vertical-temperature-time}
Let $(v,T)$ be the strong solution with the initial data assumed in
this section. For every $0<t_0<\mathcal T^*$,
\[
\partial_t\partial_zT\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)),
\qquad
\nabla_H\partial_zT\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)).
\]
More precisely, there exists a continuous nondecreasing function
$M_{T,z}$ on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$ such that
\[
\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|\nabla_H\partial_zT(s)\|_{L^2}^2
+\int_0^t\|\partial_t\partial_zT(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds
\leq M_{T,z}(t)
\]
for every $0\leq t<\mathcal T^*$.
head: environment
name: Time regularity of the vertical temperature derivative

title: Proof:
body_md:
Fix $0<t_0<\mathcal T^*$. Proposition~\ref{prop:velocity-higher-spatial},
with $\varepsilon=1/4$, and the embedding
$H^{7/4}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$ give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\|\partial_zv\|_{L^2(0,t_0;L^\infty)}
  +\|\nabla_H\cdot v\|_{L^2(0,t_0;L^\infty)}
 \leq C\|v\|_{L^2(0,t_0;H^{11/4})}<\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also, \eqref{eq:w-anisotropic-H73} implies
\[
 \|w\|_{L^2(0,t_0;L^\infty)}
 \leq C\|v\|_{L^2(0,t_0;H^{7/3})}<\infty.
\]
Section~\ref{sec:construction-global} and
Propositions~\ref{prop:velocity-H2} and~\ref{prop:Tzz-estimate}
provide
\[
\begin{gathered}
 v\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^\infty),\qquad
 \partial_zT,\ \nabla_HT\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2),\\
 \nabla_H\partial_zT\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2),\qquad
 \partial_z^2T\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2).
\end{gathered}
\]

Differentiating the temperature equation in $z$ and using
$\partial_zw=-\nabla_H\cdot v$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \partial_t\partial_zT-\Delta_H\partial_zT
 ={}&-\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT
     -v\cdot\nabla_H\partial_zT\\
    &+(\nabla_H\cdot v)\partial_zT
     -w\partial_z^2T.
\end{aligned}
\]
By H\"older's inequality,
\begin{align}
 \|\partial_zv\cdot\nabla_HT\|_{L^2}
 &\leq
 \|\partial_zv\|_{L^\infty}\|\nabla_HT\|_{L^2},
 \label{eq:Tz-1}\\
 \|v\cdot\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_{L^2}
 &\leq
 \|v\|_{L^\infty}\|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_{L^2},
 \label{eq:Tz-2}\\
 \|(\nabla_H\cdot v)\partial_zT\|_{L^2}
 &\leq
 \|\nabla_H\cdot v\|_{L^\infty}\|\partial_zT\|_{L^2},
 \label{eq:Tz-3}\\
 \|w\partial_z^2T\|_{L^2}
 &\leq
 \|w\|_{L^\infty}\|\partial_z^2T\|_{L^2}.
 \label{eq:Tz-4}
\end{align}
Thus all four terms belong to $L^2(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega))$.

Multiply the differentiated equation with $\partial_t\partial_zT$, integrate it over $\Omega$, and applying Young's inequality give,
\begin{align}
 &\frac{d}{dt}\|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_{L^2}^2
   +\|\partial_t\partial_zT\|_{L^2}^2
 \nonumber\\
 &\quad\leq C\Bigl(
   \|\partial_zv\|_{L^\infty}^2\|\nabla_HT\|_{L^2}^2
   +\|v\|_{L^\infty}^2
      \|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_{L^2}^2
 \nonumber\\
 &\hspace{27mm}
   +\|\nabla_H\cdot v\|_{L^\infty}^2
      \|\partial_zT\|_{L^2}^2
   +\|w\|_{L^\infty}^2
      \|\partial_z^2T\|_{L^2}^2
   \Bigr).
 \label{eq:Tz-energy}
\end{align}
Integrating and we obtain,
\begin{align*}
 &\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
      \|\nabla_H\partial_zT(s)\|_{L^2}^2
   +\int_0^t
      \|\partial_t\partial_zT(s)\|_{L^2}^2\,ds\\
 &\quad\leq 2\|\nabla_H\partial_zT_0\|_{L^2}^2+C\int_0^t\Bigl(
   \|\partial_zv\|_{L^\infty}^2\|\nabla_HT\|_{L^2}^2
   +\|v\|_{L^\infty}^2
      \|\nabla_H\partial_zT\|_{L^2}^2\\
 &\hspace{27mm}
   +\|\nabla_H\cdot v\|_{L^\infty}^2
      \|\partial_zT\|_{L^2}^2
   +\|w\|_{L^\infty}^2
      \|\partial_z^2T\|_{L^2}^2
   \Bigr)\,ds.
\end{align*}
Since $t_0<\mathcal T^*$ is arbitrary, the right-hand side defines a continuous nondecreasing function $M_{T,z}$ on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$, as required.

label: rem:vertical-temperature-time-justification
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:vertical-temperature-time-justification}
The preceding calculation is justified using the auxiliary Galerkin solutions $(\partial_zT)_N$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:Tzz-estimate}. Testing their equations with $\partial_t(\partial_zT)_N$, the uniform bounds established there and the coefficient bounds above give a uniform $L^2(0,t_0;L^2)$ bound for these time derivatives. Weak compactness and the previously identified limit yield $\partial_t\partial_zT\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2)$; the differentiated equation then gives $\Delta_H\partial_zT\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2)$. The time-trace theorem for the horizontal Dirichlet Laplacian therefore yields $\partial_zT\in C([0,t_0];\mathcal V_H)$ with initial value $\partial_zT_0$, and the corresponding energy identity justifies \eqref{eq:Tz-energy} and the resulting estimate at every time.

title: Proof:
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Let $(v,T)$ be the unique global strong solution provided by
Theorem~\ref{thm:global-well-posedness}, and fix an arbitrary $t_0>0$.
Propositions~\ref{prop:velocity-H2} and~\ref{prop:velocity-higher-spatial}
give
\[
 v\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^2(\Omega))
       \cap L^2(0,t_0;H^{3-\varepsilon}(\Omega))
 \qquad\text{for every }\varepsilon\in(0,1).
\]
Propositions~\ref{prop:Tzz-estimate} and
\ref{prop:horizontal-temperature-L2}, together with horizontal
Dirichlet elliptic regularity and Lemma~\ref{lem:anisotropic-isotropic},
yield $T\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^2(\Omega))$, as shown in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:horizontal-T-higher-reg}. That proposition also
gives $\nabla_HT\in L^2(0,t_0;H^2(\Omega))$.

Proposition~\ref{prop:time-derivative-L2} implies
\[
 v_t\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega)),\qquad
 T_t,\ \nabla_HT_t\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(\Omega)).
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:vertical-temperature-time} supplies the remaining vertical derivative and hence $T_t\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega))$.
Together with the spatial bounds, these estimates show that
\[
 v,T\in H^1(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega))
       \hookrightarrow C([0,t_0];H^1(\Omega)).
\]
Thus all the asserted regularities hold on every finite time interval.
Existence and uniqueness follow from
Theorem~\ref{thm:global-well-posedness}, completing the proof.

name: Weighted stability and uniqueness

title: Proof:
body_md:
We follow the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:strong-solution-stability} and record the modifications caused by the fixed depth $h$. The stated time regularity justifies testing the difference equations
by $v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}$ and $\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)}$.
With $(v^{(1)},\omega^{(1)})$ as the transporting field,
\eqref{eq:topographic-transport-skew} gives transport cancellation
in the weighted inner product. The hydrostatic constraint eliminates
pressure, and the Coriolis term vanishes as before.

By \eqref{eq:omega-representation}, the additional term is $\nabla_H\log h\cdot(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})$, and
\[
 |\omega^{(1)}-\omega^{(2)}|
 \leq C_h\int_{-1}^0
       \bigl(|\nabla_H(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})|
                         +|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}|\bigr)\,d\xi.
\]
Consequently, Lemma~\ref{anisotropic inequality} gives the same bounds for the two vertical transport terms as in Proposition~\ref{prop:strong-solution-stability}, with constants depending on $h$. The horizontal transport estimates are unchanged by weighted norm equivalence.

For the temperature term, integration by parts in physical coordinates gives
\begin{align}
 &\bigl(\mathcal B_h(\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)}),
                 v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\bigr)_h\\
 &\quad=-\bigl(\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)},
                         h(\omega^{(1)}-\omega^{(2)})\bigr)_h\\
 &\qquad\phantom{=}-\bigl(\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)},
              \sigma(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\cdot\nabla_Hh\bigr)_h.
\end{align}
Here $h(\omega^{(1)}-\omega^{(2)}) +\sigma(v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\cdot\nabla_Hh$ is the pullback of the difference of the physical vertical velocities. The preceding diagnostic bound therefore yields

\begin{align}
 &\bigl|\bigl(\mathcal B_h(\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)}),
                 v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\bigr)_h\bigr|\\
 &\qquad\leq C_h\|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)}\|_{2,h}
                        \|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_{H^1}.
\end{align}

The remaining Sobolev and Young estimates are those of Proposition~\ref{prop:strong-solution-stability}. Using coercivity of $\mathfrak a_{v,h}$ to absorb the dissipation terms, and bounding the resulting coefficients by \eqref{eq:topographic-stability-coefficient}, we obtain
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(\|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_{2,h}^2
                  +\|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)}\|_{2,h}^2\Bigr)\\
 &\quad+\mathfrak a_{v,h}
                  (v^{(1)}-v^{(2)},v^{(1)}-v^{(2)})\\
 &\quad+\|\nabla_H(\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)})\|_{2,h}^2\\
 &\leq\Lambda_h[v^{(2)},\theta^{(2)}]
       \Bigl(\|v^{(1)}-v^{(2)}\|_{2,h}^2
                  +\|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(2)}\|_{2,h}^2\Bigr).
\end{split}
\label{eq:topographic-stability-energy}
\end{equation}
The strong-solution bounds imply
$\Lambda_h[v^{(2)},\theta^{(2)}]\in L^1(0,t_0)$.
Multiplication by the integrating factor and integration give
\eqref{eq:topographic-strong-stability}.
Time continuity in $L_h^2$ yields the estimate for every
$t\in[0,t_0]$, and hence uniqueness and continuous dependence.

label: prop:varying-bottom-main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{prop:varying-bottom-main}
Assume \eqref{eq:h-assumptions} and $h\in C^3(\overline M)$.
Consider the varying-bottom problem with the thermal diffusion operator
$A_{T,h}$ defined in \eqref{eq:topographic-laplacian} and the original
velocity and lateral temperature boundary conditions.\\
\smallskip
\noindent\textup{(i) Global strong solutions.}
For every $(v_0^{\mathrm{phys}},T_0)\in V_h\times V_{T,h}$,
there exists a unique global strong solution. For every finite $t_0>0$,
its pullbacks $v=v^{\mathrm{phys}}\circ\Phi$ and $\theta=T\circ\Phi$
satisfy
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 v\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1(Q)^2)\cap L^2(0,t_0;H^2(Q)^2),
 \qquad v_t\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(Q)^2),\\
 \theta\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1(Q)),\qquad
 \nabla_H\theta\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(Q)),\\
 \theta_t\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2(Q)).
 \end{gathered}
\]

\smallskip
\noindent\textup{(ii) Persistence of higher regularity.}
Suppose, in addition, that $M$ has $C^3$ boundary and
$\partial_\nu h=0$ on $\partial M$, where $\nu$ is the horizontal
outward unit normal; this is condition \eqref{eq:top-stokes-orthogonal}.
Assume also that
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 v_0^{\mathrm{phys}}\in H^2(\Omega_h)^2\cap V_h,
 \qquad T_0\in H^2(\Omega_h)\cap V_{T,h},\\
 \partial_zv_0^{\mathrm{phys}}=0\quad\text{on }\Gamma_t.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Then the temperature satisfies
\eqref{eq:topographic-physical-H2-conclusion}. For every finite $t_0>0$
and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, the velocity satisfies
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 v^{\mathrm{phys}}\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^2(\Omega_h)^2)
                 \cap C([0,t_0];H^1(\Omega_h)^2),\\
  v^{\mathrm{phys}}\in L^2(0,t_0;H^{3-\varepsilon}(\Omega_h)^2),
 \qquad v_t^{\mathrm{phys}}\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1(\Omega_h)^2).
 \end{gathered}
\]
No top or bottom temperature boundary condition is imposed.
The constants may depend on the fixed domain, $h_*$, $h^*$,
and $\|h\|_{C^3}$, in addition to the initial norms and the time interval.

name: Varying bottom topography

label: prop:top-time-derivative-L2
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
We follow the difference-quotient argument of
Proposition~\ref{prop:time-derivative-L2}, using
Proposition~\ref{prop:topographic-strong-stability}
for the weighted stability estimate.

Fix $t_0,\eta_0>0$ and consider the existing strong solution
on $[0,t_0+\eta_0]$. For $0<\eta<\eta_0$, set
\[
 \delta_\eta v(t):=\frac{v(t+\eta)-v(t)}{\eta},
 \qquad
 \delta_\eta\theta(t):=
             \frac{\theta(t+\eta)-\theta(t)}{\eta}.
\]
The initial regularity and boundary conditions imply
$v_0\in D(\mathcal A_{v,h})$ and $\theta_0\in D(A_h)$.
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_v&:=P_h\bigl[
       \mathcal L_hv_0-L_{v_0}v_0-f_0k\times v_0
                         +\mathcal B_h\theta_0\bigr],\\
 R_\theta&:=-A_h\theta_0-L_{v_0}\theta_0,
 \qquad
 E_0:=\|R_v\|_{2,h}^2+\|R_\theta\|_{2,h}^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
By \eqref{eq:topographic-anisotropic-product},
\eqref{eq:topographic-basic-buoyancy-bound}, and
$H^2(Q)\hookrightarrow L^\infty(Q)$, both residuals
belong to $L_h^2$, with
\begin{equation}
 E_0\leq C_{h,f_0}
       \bigl(1+\|v_0\|_{H^2}^2\bigr)
       \bigl(\|v_0\|_{H^2}^2+\|\theta_0\|_{H^2}^2\bigr).
 \label{eq:top-time-initial}
\end{equation}

We first estimate the initial difference quotients.
The equations for $v-v_0$ and $\theta-\theta_0$
have the same structure as the difference equations in
Proposition~\ref{prop:topographic-strong-stability},
with reference pair $(v_0,\theta_0)$ and additional
forcing $(R_v,R_\theta)$.
Repeating the energy calculation in its proof and retaining
these forcing terms gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\frac{d}{dt}
       \bigl(\|v-v_0\|_{2,h}^2
                         +\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{2,h}^2\bigr)\\
 &\quad\leq
 C_{0,h}\bigl(\|v-v_0\|_{2,h}^2
                         +\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{2,h}^2\bigr)\\
 &\qquad\quad
 +2\sqrt{E_0}\,
       \bigl(\|v-v_0\|_{2,h}^2
                         +\|\theta-\theta_0\|_{2,h}^2\bigr)^{1/2},
\end{aligned}
\]
where $C_{0,h}$ depends only on the initial $H^2$ norms
and the fixed coefficients.
The known $H^1_tL_h^2$ regularity makes the energy
absolutely continuous, and its initial value is zero.
Lemma~\ref{lem:sqrt-gronwall} therefore yields
\[
 \bigl(\|v(s)-v_0\|_{2,h}^2
                    +\|\theta(s)-\theta_0\|_{2,h}^2\bigr)^{1/2}
 \leq s\sqrt{E_0}\,e^{C_{0,h}s/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \|\delta_\eta v(0)\|_{2,h}^2
       +\|\delta_\eta\theta(0)\|_{2,h}^2
 \leq E_0e^{C_{0,h}\eta}.
 \label{eq:top-time-initial-quotients}
\end{equation}
No initial trace of $(v_t,\theta_t)$ is used.

Since the system is autonomous, both
$(v(\,\cdot+\eta),\theta(\,\cdot+\eta))$ and
$(v,\theta)$ solve the same equations on $[0,t_0]$.
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:topographic-strong-stability}
with these as the first and second solutions, respectively.
Set
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda_h(s):=\Lambda_h[v,\theta](s),
 \label{eq:top-time-coefficient}
\end{equation}
where the expression on the right is defined in
\eqref{eq:topographic-stability-coefficient}.
This coefficient is independent of $\eta$ and belongs to
$L^1(0,t_0)$ by the previously established $H^1$ bounds.
Dividing \eqref{eq:topographic-strong-stability} by $\eta^2$
and using \eqref{eq:top-time-initial-quotients}, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
       \bigl(\|\delta_\eta v(s)\|_{2,h}^2
                   +\|\delta_\eta\theta(s)\|_{2,h}^2\bigr)\\
 &\quad+\int_0^t
       \Bigl(\mathfrak a_{v,h}(\delta_\eta v,\delta_\eta v)
                   +\|\nabla_H\delta_\eta\theta\|_{2,h}^2\Bigr)\,ds\\
 &\qquad\leq
 2E_0\exp\!\left(C_{0,h}\eta+\int_0^t\Lambda_h(s)\,ds\right),
 \qquad 0\leq t\leq t_0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the factor $2$ results from estimating the supremum
and the dissipation integral separately.

Finally, the known $H^1_tL_h^2$ regularity gives
\[
 \delta_\eta v(t)=\frac1\eta\int_t^{t+\eta}v_t(s)\,ds,
 \qquad
 \delta_\eta\theta(t)=
                 \frac1\eta\int_t^{t+\eta}\theta_t(s)\,ds.
\]
As in Proposition~\ref{prop:time-derivative-L2},
the strong convergence of these Steklov averages yields
\[
 (\delta_\eta v,\delta_\eta\theta)
 \longrightarrow(v_t,\theta_t)
 \quad\text{strongly in }L^2(0,t_0;L_h^2)
 \quad\text{as }\eta\downarrow0.
\]
The uniform estimate also gives, along a subsequence,
weak convergence in the velocity and horizontal temperature
form spaces and weak-star convergence in
$L^\infty(0,t_0;L_h^2)$.
The strong convergence identifies these limits with the
time derivatives, and the form-domain constraints pass
to the limit by weak closedness.
Lower semicontinuity therefore gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}_{0<s<t}
       \bigl(\|v_t(s)\|_{2,h}^2+\|\theta_t(s)\|_{2,h}^2\bigr)\\
 &\quad+\int_0^t
       \Bigl(\mathfrak a_{v,h}(v_t,v_t)
                         +\|\nabla_H\theta_t\|_{2,h}^2\Bigr)\,ds\\
 &\qquad\leq
 2E_0\exp\!\left(\int_0^t\Lambda_h(s)\,ds\right).
\end{split}
\label{eq:top-time-gronwall}
\end{equation}
Since $t_0$ is arbitrary, we may take
\[
 M_{4,h}(t):=
 2(1+E_0)\exp\!\left(\int_0^t\Lambda_h(s)\,ds\right),
\]
which is continuous, nondecreasing, and finite on every
finite time interval.
The physical-coordinate estimate follows from
\eqref{eq:top-time-velocity-form} and
$(X^hT_t)\circ\Phi=\nabla_H\theta_t$.

title: Remark

initial residual $E_0$ in \eqref{eq:top-time-initial};
all time-dependent coefficients in the proof are controlled at the
previously established $H^1$ level.
