name: Higher hydrostatic Stokes estimate at orthogonal junctions

label: eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift
title: Proof:
body_md:
We first recall the scalar estimate
\begin{equation}
 \|g\|_{H^{2+a}(\Omega_h)}
 \leq C_{h,a}\bigl(\|-\Delta g\|_{H^a(\Omega_h)}
 +\|g\|_{H^1(\Omega_h)}\bigr),
 \qquad 0<a<1,
 \label{eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift}
\end{equation}
for the homogeneous scalar boundary conditions in
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-system}. Even reflection across $z=0$, using the
top Neumann condition, gives a homogeneous Dirichlet problem on
\[
 \widetilde\Omega_h
 =\{(x,y,z):(x,y)\in M,\ -h(x,y)<z<h(x,y)\}.
\]
By \eqref{eq:top-stokes-orthogonal}, its upper and lower faces meet the sidewall at right angles. The boundary has $C^3$ faces and edges, with no vertices, and the Dirichlet edge exponent is $2$.For background on the dependence of scalar elliptic corner regularity on the opening angles and boundary conditions, see \cite[Chapters~4--5]{Grisvard2011}.
Let $S$ be the bounded linear Dirichlet solution operator. 
\[
 \begin{cases}
 -\Delta(S\phi)=\phi&\text{in }\widetilde\Omega_h,\\
 S\phi=0&\text{on }\partial\widetilde\Omega_h.
 \end{cases}
\]
For $p_0=4/(2-a)$ and $p_1=4/(3-a)$,
\cite[Theorem~3.2 and Corollary~3.7]{Dauge92} therefore gives
\[
 S:L^{p_0}\longrightarrow W^{2,p_0},\qquad
 S:W^{1,p_1}\longrightarrow W^{3,p_1}.
\]
Indeed, $2-2/p_0<2$ and $3-2/p_1<2$, and $C^3$ faces suffice.
Since $(1-a)/p_0+a/p_1=1/2$, complex interpolation, as in
Lemma~\ref{lemma:Gagliardo}\textup{(ii)}, yields
$S:H^a\to H^{2+a}$. Even reflection of the forcing is bounded in
$H^a$ for $0<a<1$; restricting the solution to $\Omega_h$ proves
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift}. This argument also covers constant
depth, when $\widetilde\Omega_h=M\times(-h_0,h_0)$.

\emph{Constant depth.}
Write $\Omega=M\times(-h,0)$, where $h>0$ is constant.
Lemma~\ref{lem:top-stokes-H2} first gives
\[
 \|v\|_{H^2(\Omega)}+\|p_s\|_{H^1(M)}
 \leq C_h\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
\]
In particular, the bottom trace of $\partial_zv$ is well defined and
\[
 \|\partial_zv|_{z=-h}\|_{H^{1/2}(M)}
 \leq C_h\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
\]
Using the normalized averages
$\bar v=h^{-1}\int_{-h}^0v\,dz$ and
$\bar f=h^{-1}\int_{-h}^0f\,dz$, integration of
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-system} in $z$ yields
\begin{align}
 -\Delta_H\bar v+\nabla_Hp_s
 &=\bar f-h^{-1}\partial_zv|_{z=-h}
 &&\text{in }M,\label{eq:barv}\\
 \nabla_H\cdot\bar v&=0
 &&\text{in }M,\label{eq:barv-div}\\
 \bar v&=0
 &&\text{on }\partial M.\nonumber
\end{align}
Here the top derivative vanishes by the prescribed Neumann condition.
This averaging only uses the first-derivative traces already supplied
by the $H^2$ estimate.

The Dirichlet Stokes estimates on the smooth planar domain $M$,
together with fractional interpolation, imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\nabla_Hp_s\|_{H^{1/2}(M)}
 &\leq C_h\left(
       \|\bar f\|_{H^{1/2}(M)}
       +\|\partial_zv|_{z=-h}\|_{H^{1/2}(M)}\right)\\
 &\leq C_h\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega)};
 \end{aligned}
\]
see \cite[Chapter~IV]{Galdi11} and \cite{BerghLofstrom76}.
Since $p_s$ is independent of $z$, the scalar equation
$-\Delta v=f-\nabla_Hp_s$ and
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift} with $a=1/2$ give
\[
 \|v\|_{H^{5/2}(\Omega)}
 \leq C_h\left(
       \|f\|_{H^{1/2}(\Omega)}
       +\|\nabla_Hp_s\|_{H^{1/2}(M)}
       +\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\right)
 \leq C_h\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega)}.
\]
The trace theorem now yields
\[
 \|\partial_zv|_{z=-h}\|_{H^1(M)}
 \leq C_h\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega)}.
\]
Applying the planar Stokes estimate once more to
\eqref{eq:barv}--\eqref{eq:barv-div}, with the same homogeneous
Dirichlet condition, gives
\[
 \|\nabla_Hp_s\|_{H^1(M)}
 \leq C_h\left(
       \|\bar f\|_{H^1(M)}
       +\|\partial_zv|_{z=-h}\|_{H^1(M)}\right)
 \leq C_h\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega)}.
\]
Finally, for every $0<\varepsilon<1$, apply
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift} with $a=1-\varepsilon$ to
$-\Delta v=f-\nabla_Hp_s$. Together with
$\|\partial_zv\|_{H^{2-\varepsilon}(\Omega)}
\leq C\|v\|_{H^{3-\varepsilon}(\Omega)}$, this proves
\[
 \|v\|_{H^{3-\varepsilon}(\Omega)}
 +\|\partial_zv\|_{H^{2-\varepsilon}(\Omega)}
 +\|\nabla_Hp_s\|_{H^{1-\varepsilon}(M)}
 \leq C_{h,\varepsilon}\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega)}.
\]


\emph{Variable depth.}
Fix $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and use the normalized average $M_h$
defined in Subsection~\ref{subsec:topographic-notation}.
Tangential differentiation of the bottom condition gives
\[
 (\partial_i v)_b=(\partial_i h)(\partial_zv)_b,
 \qquad i=1,2,
\]
where the subscript $b$ denotes restriction to $z=-h(x,y)$.
Consequently, Leibniz' rule and the top condition $\partial_zv=0$
yield
\[
 \int_{-h(x,y)}^0\Delta v\,dz
 =\Delta_H(hM_hv)-(1+|\nabla_Hh|^2)(\partial_zv)_b.
\]
Integration of \eqref{eq:top-stokes-system} therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 -\Delta_H(hM_hv)+\nabla_H(hp_s)
 ={}&hM_hf-(1+|\nabla_Hh|^2)(\partial_zv)_b
       +p_s\nabla_Hh,\\
 \nabla_H\cdot(hM_hv)={}&0,
 \qquad (hM_hv)|_{\partial M}=0.
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:top-stokes-higher-average}
\end{equation}
The bottom derivative is retained; no homogeneous condition on
$(\partial_zv)_b$ is used.
Lemma~\ref{lem:top-stokes-H2}, the trace theorem, and the boundedness
of vertical averaging give
\[
 \|(\partial_zv)_b\|_{H^{1/2}(M)}
 +\|hM_hf\|_{H^1(M)}+\|p_s\nabla_Hh\|_{H^1(M)}
 \leq C_h\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega_h)}.
\]
Apply the planar Dirichlet Stokes estimate to
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-higher-average}, with velocity $hM_hv$ and
pressure $hp_s$. Using
$\nabla_Hp_s=h^{-1}[\nabla_H(hp_s)-p_s\nabla_Hh]$, we obtain
\[
 \|\nabla_Hp_s\|_{H^{1/2-\varepsilon}(M)}
 \leq C_{h,\varepsilon}\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega_h)};
\]
see \cite[Chapter~IV]{Galdi11} and \cite{BerghLofstrom76}.
Apply \eqref{eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift} with
$a=1/2-\varepsilon$ to $-\Delta v=f-\nabla_Hp_s$ and then take
the bottom trace. This gives
\[
 \|v\|_{H^{5/2-\varepsilon}(\Omega_h)}
 +\|(\partial_zv)_b\|_{H^{1-\varepsilon}(M)}
 \leq C_{h,\varepsilon}\|f\|_{H^1(\Omega_h)}.
\]
A second application of the planar Stokes estimate to
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-higher-average} gives the same bound for
$\|\nabla_Hp_s\|_{H^{1-\varepsilon}(M)}$. Finally,
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-scalar-shift} with $a=1-\varepsilon$ yields
\eqref{eq:top-stokes-higher}. The cases $1/2\leq\varepsilon<1$
follow by Sobolev embedding from any smaller loss, for example
$\varepsilon=1/4$.

label: lem:sqrt-gronwall
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:sqrt-gronwall}
Let $\tau>0$, let $Y:[0,\tau]\to[0,\infty)$ be absolutely continuous, and let $a,b\in L^1(0,\tau)$ be nonnegative. Suppose that
\[
Y'(t)\leq a(t)Y(t)+2b(t)\sqrt{Y(t)}
\qquad\text{for a.e. }t\in(0,\tau).
\]
Then, for every $t\in[0,\tau]$,
\[
\sqrt{Y(t)}
\leq
\sqrt{Y(0)}
\exp\left(\frac12\int_0^t a(r)\,dr\right)
+
\int_0^t b(s)
\exp\left(\frac12\int_s^t a(r)\,dr\right)\,ds.
\]
In particular, if $Y(0)=0$, $a(t)\equiv a_0\geq0$,
and $b(t)\equiv b_0\geq0$, then
\[
\sqrt{Y(t)}\leq b_0t\,e^{a_0t/2},
\qquad
Y(t)\leq b_0^2t^2e^{a_0t},
\qquad 0\leq t\leq\tau.
\]
head: environment
name: Square-root Gronwall inequality

title: Proof:
body_md:
For $\varepsilon>0$, set
\[
Z_\varepsilon(t):=\sqrt{Y(t)+\varepsilon}.
\]
Then $Z_\varepsilon$ is absolutely continuous and strictly
positive. The chain rule gives, for almost every $t$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
Z_\varepsilon'(t)
&=\frac{Y'(t)}{2\sqrt{Y(t)+\varepsilon}}\\
&\leq
\frac{a(t)}{2}
\frac{Y(t)}{\sqrt{Y(t)+\varepsilon}}
+
b(t)\frac{\sqrt{Y(t)}}{\sqrt{Y(t)+\varepsilon}}\\
&\leq \frac{a(t)}{2}Z_\varepsilon(t)+b(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiplying by the integrating factor
$\exp(-\frac12\int_0^t a(r)\,dr)$ yields
\[
\frac{d}{dt}
\left[
\exp\left(-\frac12\int_0^t a(r)\,dr\right)
Z_\varepsilon(t)
\right]
\leq
b(t)\exp\left(-\frac12\int_0^t a(r)\,dr\right).
\]
Integrating from $0$ to $t$, and using
$Z_\varepsilon(0)=\sqrt{Y(0)+\varepsilon}$, we obtain
\[
Z_\varepsilon(t)
\leq
\sqrt{Y(0)+\varepsilon}
\exp\left(\frac12\int_0^t a(r)\,dr\right)
+
\int_0^t b(s)
\exp\left(\frac12\int_s^t a(r)\,dr\right)\,ds.
\]
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ proves the first assertion.
For constant coefficients and $Y(0)=0$, it follows that
\[
\sqrt{Y(t)}
\leq b_0\int_0^t e^{a_0(t-s)/2}\,ds
\leq b_0t\,e^{a_0t/2}.
\]
Squaring gives the remaining estimate.

label: lem:anisotropic-isotropic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:anisotropic-isotropic}
Let $\Omega=M\times(-h,0)$, where $M\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is a bounded
$C^3$ domain. Let $0<s\leq2$. Suppose that
\[
    f\in L^2((-h,0);H^s(M))
\]
and
\[
    f,\ \partial_z f,\ \partial_z^2f\in L^2(\Omega).
\]
Then $f\in H^s(\Omega)$ and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:anisotropic-isotropic}
    \|f\|_{H^s(\Omega)}
    \le C
    \left(
        \|f\|_{L^2_zH^s_H}
        +
        \|f\|_{H^2_zL^2_H}
    \right),
\end{equation}
where
\[
    \|f\|_{H^2_zL^2_H}^2
    :=
    \|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2
    +
    \|\partial_zf\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2
    +
    \|\partial_z^2f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.
\]
head: environment
name: Anisotropic-to-isotropic Sobolev estimate

title: Proof:
body_md:
Since $M$ is smooth and bounded and $(-h,0)$ is a bounded interval,
the standard Sobolev extension theorem, applied in the horizontal
and vertical variables, gives an extension $\widetilde f$ of $f$ to
$\mathbb{R}^3$ such that
\[
    \|\widetilde f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R};H^s(\mathbb{R}^2))}
    \le
    C\|f\|_{L^2((-h,0);H^s(M))}
\]
and
\[
    \|\widetilde f\|_{H^2(\mathbb{R};L^2(\mathbb{R}^2))}
    \le
    C\|f\|_{H^2_zL^2_H}.
\]
We may therefore apply the Fourier transform to $\widetilde f$.
Writing $\xi=(\xi_H,\xi_3)$, where
$\xi_H=(\xi_1,\xi_2)$, and using $0<s\leq2$, we have
\[
    (1+|\xi_H|^2+|\xi_3|^2)^s
    \le
    C_s\left[
        (1+|\xi_H|^2)^s
        +(1+|\xi_3|^2)^2
    \right].
\]
Hence, by Plancherel's theorem,
\begin{align*}
    \|\widetilde f\|_{H^s(\mathbb{R}^3)}^2
    &\le
    C_s
    \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}
    (1+|\xi_H|^2)^s
    |\widehat{\widetilde f}(\xi)|^2\,d\xi
    \\
    &\quad
    +C_s
    \int_{\mathbb{R}^3}
    (1+|\xi_3|^2)^2
    |\widehat{\widetilde f}(\xi)|^2\,d\xi
    \\
    &\le
    C_s
    \left(
        \|\widetilde f\|_{L^2_zH^s_H}^2
        +
        \|\widetilde f\|_{H^2_zL^2_H}^2
    \right).
\end{align*}
Restricting $\widetilde f$ back to $\Omega$ gives
\eqref{eq:anisotropic-isotropic}.

label: lem:weighted-vertical-temperature
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:weighted-vertical-temperature}
Let $Q_\ell=M\times(-\ell,0)$, where $\ell>0$ and $M$ is a bounded
$C^3$ domain, and let $\rho\in C^3(\overline M)$ be positive. Write
\[
 \|g\|_{2,\rho}^2=\int_{Q_\ell}\rho|g|^2,
 \qquad A_\rho=-\rho^{-1}\nabla_H\cdot(\rho\nabla_H),
\]
with horizontal Dirichlet form domain
$L^2((-\ell,0);H_0^1(M))$. Suppose that
\[
 v\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^2(Q_\ell)^2)
       \cap L^2(0,t_0;H^{11/4}(Q_\ell)^2),
 \qquad v|_{\partial M\times(-\ell,0)}=0,
\]
and that
\[
 \omega(\sigma)=-\rho^{-1}\int_{-\ell}^{\sigma}
                       \nabla_H\cdot(\rho v)(s)\,ds,
 \qquad \omega|_{\sigma=0}=0.
\]
Let $\theta$ solve
\[
 \theta_t+A_\rho\theta+v\cdot\nabla_H\theta
                   +\omega\partial_\sigma\theta=0
\]
in distributions, with zero lateral trace, initial value
$\theta_0\in H^2(Q_\ell)$ with zero lateral trace, and
\[
 \theta\in L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1),\qquad
 \nabla_H\theta\in L^2(0,t_0;H^1),\qquad
 \theta_t\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2).
\]
No temperature condition is imposed at $\sigma=-\ell,0$.
Then
\[
 \partial_{\sigma\sigma}\theta\in L^\infty(0,t_0;L^2),
 \qquad
 \nabla_H\partial_{\sigma\sigma}\theta\in L^2(0,t_0;L^2).
\]
More precisely, for $0\leq t\leq t_0$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
       \|\partial_{\sigma\sigma}\theta(s)\|_{2,\rho}^2
       +\int_0^t\|\nabla_H\partial_{\sigma\sigma}\theta\|_{2,\rho}^2\,ds\\
 &\qquad\leq C\bigl(1+\|\partial_{\sigma\sigma}\theta_0\|_{2,\rho}^2\bigr)
        \exp\!\Bigg(C\int_0^t\|v(s)\|_{H^{11/4}}\\
 &\hspace{16mm}\cdot\bigl(1+\|\theta\|_{L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1)}
             +\|\nabla_H\theta(s)\|_{H^1}\bigr)\,ds\Bigg),
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:weighted-vertical-temperature-bound}
\end{equation}
where $C$ depends only on $M,\ell,\rho$. The supremum uses the
weakly $L^2$-continuous representative of the second derivative.
head: environment
name: Vertical temperature regularity with a fixed horizontal weight

title: Proof:
body_md:
This is the fixed-weight version of Proposition~\ref{prop:Tzz-estimate};
the varying-bottom case corresponds to $\ell=1$ and $\rho=h$.
We record only the changes in its proof. With
$(f,g)_\rho=\int_{Q_\ell}\rho fg$, positivity of $\rho$ gives equivalence
of weighted and unweighted norms, while
\[
 (A_\rho f,g)_\rho=(\nabla_Hf,\nabla_Hg)_\rho,
 \qquad [\partial_\sigma,A_\rho]=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \nabla_H\cdot(\rho v)+\partial_\sigma(\rho\omega)=0,
 \qquad \omega|_{\sigma=-\ell,0}=0,
\]
so the principal transport cancels in the weighted energy identity.
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \partial_\sigma\omega
   &=-\nabla_H\cdot v-\nabla_H\log\rho\cdot v,\\
 \partial_{\sigma\sigma}\omega
   &=-\nabla_H\cdot\partial_\sigma v
     -\nabla_H\log\rho\cdot\partial_\sigma v.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The additional terms contain the fixed coefficient
$\nabla_H\log\rho\in C^2(\overline M)$ and lower-order derivatives of $v$. Hence the coefficient bound \eqref{eq:flat-vertical-coefficients} and the product estimates in Proposition~\ref{prop:Tzz-estimate} remain valid with $(z,w,T)$ replaced by $(\sigma,\omega,\theta)$ and constants depending
on $M,\ell,\rho$.

Repeating that proof in $L^2_\rho$, with $r=\partial_{\sigma\sigma}\theta$,
gives the same energy inequality
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d}{dt}\bigl(1+\|r\|_{2,\rho}^2\bigr)
       +2\|\nabla_Hr\|_{2,\rho}^2
 \leq a_\rho(t)\bigl(1+\|r\|_{2,\rho}^2\bigr),
 \label{eq:weighted-vertical-energy}
\end{equation}
where
\[
 a_\rho(t)=C\|v(t)\|_{H^{11/4}}
 \bigl(1+\|\theta\|_{L^\infty(0,t_0;H^1)}
           +\|\nabla_H\theta(t)\|_{H^1}\bigr)
 \in L^1(0,t_0).
\]
Gronwall's inequality yields \eqref{eq:weighted-vertical-temperature-bound}.
As in the cited proposition, the supremum is taken over the weakly
$L^2_\rho$-continuous representative; no vertical endpoint condition
on $\theta$ is used.

label: prop:appendix-basic-energy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:appendix-basic-energy}
For every $0<t<\mathcal T^*$,
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|v(s)\|_2^2
 +\int_0^t\|\nabla v(s)\|_2^2\,ds
 \leq C\left(\|v_0\|_2^2+\int_0^t\|T(s)\|_2^2\,ds\right)
 \leq C\left(\|v_0\|_2^2+t\|T_0\|_2^2\right),
\]
where $C$ depends only on $M$ and $h$. Moreover, whenever
$T_0\in L^q(\Omega)$, $2\leq q\leq\infty$,
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|T(s)\|_q\leq\|T_0\|_q.
\]

title: Proof:
body_md:
Set $Q_T(x,y,z)=\int_{-h}^zT(x,y,\xi)\,d\xi$.
Multiply the momentum equation with $v$, 
\[
 \int_\Omega\nabla_Hp_s\cdot v
 =-\int_Mp_s\nabla_H\cdot\left(\int_{-h}^0v\,dz\right)=0.
\]
Integration by parts, yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|v\|_2^2+\|\nabla v\|_2^2
 &=\int_\Omega\nabla_H Q_T\cdot v
 =-\int_\Omega Q_T\,\nabla_H\cdot v\\
 &\leq C_h\|T\|_2\|\nabla_Hv\|_2
 \leq\frac12\|\nabla_Hv\|_2^2+C_h\|T\|_2^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d}{dt}\|v\|_2^2+\|\nabla_Hv\|_2^2
       +2\|\partial_zv\|_2^2\leq C_h\|T\|_2^2.
\end{equation}
For $2\leq q<\infty$, testing the temperature equation with
$|T|^{q-2}T$ gives
\begin{equation}
 \frac1q\frac{d}{dt}\|T\|_q^q
 +(q-1)\int_\Omega |T|^{q-2}|\nabla_HT|^2=0.
\end{equation}
Thus the $L^q$ norm is nonincreasing. For bounded $T_0$, letting
$q\to\infty$ on the bounded domain gives
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|T(s)\|_\infty\leq\|T_0\|_\infty.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
 \|T(t)\|_2^2+2\int_0^t\|\nabla_HT(s)\|_2^2\,ds
 \leq\|T_0\|_2^2.
\]
Integrating the velocity inequality and taking the time supremum
proves the first assertion. The identities are justified by the
energy approximations used in the construction.

label: prop:appendix-velocity-L6-vertical
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:appendix-velocity-L6-vertical}
Assume $v_0\in V$ and $T_0\in V_T$. There exists a continuous
nondecreasing function $M_1$ on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$ such that
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}
       \bigl(\|v(s)\|_6^2+\|u(s)\|_2^2\bigr)
 +\int_0^t\|\nabla u(s)\|_2^2\,ds\leq M_1(t).
\]
If $\mathcal T^*<\infty$, this bound remains finite as
$t\uparrow\mathcal T^*$.
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
On the existing interval of the solution, write
\[
 v_t+(v\cdot\nabla_H)v+w\partial_zv-\Delta v+\nabla_Hp_s=f,
 \qquad
 f:=\nabla_H\int_{-h}^zT\,d\xi-f_0k\times v.
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-basic-energy} and Poincar\'e's inequality imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \int_0^t\|f(s)\|_2^2\,ds
 &\leq C\int_0^t
              \bigl(\|\nabla_HT(s)\|_2^2+\|v(s)\|_2^2\bigr)\,ds\\
 &\leq C\left(\|v_0\|_2^2+(1+t)\|T_0\|_2^2\right),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where $C$ also depends on the fixed Coriolis parameter.
The forced velocity estimates of \cite{Kukavica_2007}, with
$v_0\in V$ and $f\in L^2_tL^2_x$, therefore give the assertion;
see also \cite[Theorem~2.1]{KukavicaZiane1}.
If $\mathcal T^*<\infty$, the displayed estimate first gives
$f\in L^2(0,\mathcal T^*;L^2)$. Extend this actual force by zero to
$(0,\mathcal T^*+1)$ and apply the forced velocity theorem there.
Uniqueness identifies its solution with $v$ before $\mathcal T^*$,
so the resulting bounds are uniform up to that time.

label: prop:appendix-velocity-H1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:appendix-velocity-H1}
Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-velocity-L6-vertical}, there exists
a continuous nondecreasing function $M_2$ on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$
such that
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|A^{1/2}v(s)\|_H^2
 +\int_0^t\|Av(s)\|_H^2\,ds\leq M_2(t).
\]
If $\mathcal T^*<\infty$, this bound remains finite as
$t\uparrow\mathcal T^*$.
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Testing the projected momentum equation with $Av$ and applying
the Sobolev and anisotropic product estimates gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac12\frac{d}{dt}L^2+\|Av\|_H^2
 &\leq\frac14\|Av\|_H^2
 +C\bigl(\|v\|_6^2L\|Av\|_H
          +L\|Av\|_H\|u\|_2\|\nabla u\|_2\\
 &\hspace{42mm}+\|v\|_2^2+\|\nabla_HT\|_2^2\bigr).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the $H^2$ Stokes estimate controls the second derivatives of
$v$, and the Poincar\'e estimate for $u$ uses its zero top trace.
Young's inequality therefore yields
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \frac{d}{dt}\|A^{1/2}v\|_H^2+\|Av\|_H^2
 &\leq C\bigl(\|v\|_6^4+\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla u\|_2^2\bigr)
                         \|A^{1/2}v\|_H^2\\
 &\quad+C\bigl(\|v\|_2^2+\|\nabla_HT\|_2^2\bigr).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The coefficient and the last two terms are integrable by
Propositions~\ref{prop:appendix-basic-energy}
and~\ref{prop:appendix-velocity-L6-vertical}. Gronwall's inequality proves the result.

label: prop:appendix-temperature-H1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:appendix-temperature-H1}
Assume $v_0\in V$ and $T_0\in V_T$. There exists a continuous
nondecreasing function $M_3$ on $[0,\mathcal T^*)$ such that
\[
 \sup_{0\leq s\leq t}\|\nabla T(s)\|_2^2
 +\int_0^t\|\nabla_H\nabla T(s)\|_2^2\,ds\leq M_3(t).
\]
If $\mathcal T^*<\infty$, this bound remains finite as
$t\uparrow\mathcal T^*$.
head: environment

title: Proof:
body_md:
Apply the temperature $H^1$ calculation in
Proposition~\ref{thm:H1 T} with the transporting velocity $v$.
Its coefficient is bounded by
\[
 C\bigl[1+\|v\|_{H^1}^4
        +(1+\|v\|_{H^1}^2)\|v\|_{H^2}^2\bigr],
\]
which belongs to $L^1(0,t)$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-velocity-H1} and the
$H^2$ Stokes estimate. Since $T_0\in V_T$, Gronwall's inequality
gives the assertion.
